title: W15-B/VC-5: pure timeline lane model over observed source intervals and native-confirmed ownership/grouping edges (lanes per owner or provider, open intervals stay open, measured concurrency, zoom/pan cell math, clock and gap notes); inspector wiring excluded
description:

Never infer exact timing from text or assume clocks agree; note uncertain clocks or event gaps." ObservationProjection already exposes every read needed: window({scope,invocationId,offset,limit}) -> {nodes,total,revision} with ObservedNode.interval {startedAt,endedAt?} (src/workbench/observation.ts:448), relations({scope,to,limit}) returning incoming typed edges with provenance (:397) and relationRevision() (:467). wb-6ze.1 (in progress) owns workflow-inspector.ts for the overview tree and graph fan-out and leaves the timeline branch untouched; wb-6ze.2 adds ancestor counts in observation.ts; wb-6ze.4 ranks bottlenecks and estimates a critical path. None of them computes lanes, concurrency or the zoom/pan window.

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/timeline.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-timeline.test.ts; register and wire nothing; do not edit src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts (wb-6ze.1 in flight), src/workbench/observation.ts (wb-6ze.2), src/workbench/designer.ts (reserved 07:00Z), src/index.ts or src/ui/workflow-dialog.ts.

• export const TIMELINE_CONTRACT = 'workbench.timeline/v1'; export type TimelineReader = Pick<ObservationProjection,'window'|'relations'|'relationRevision'>.
• export interface TimelineRequest { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId: string; offset: number; limit: number (1..100, the window cap); zoom: number (safe integer 1..8, cells per second); pan: number (safe integer >= 0, cells); columns: number (safe integer 8..200, bar cells); maxLanes?: number (1..64, default 16); maxRowsPerLane?: number (1..100, default 40); relationLimit?: number (1..100, default 40) }. Invalid values throw CapabilityError('validation') before any reader call.
• export function buildTimelineLanes(reader: TimelineReader, request: TimelineRequest): TimelineModel — pure, synchronous, deterministic (no Date.now, Math.random, process or environment reads; every timestamp comes from reader rows), calls reader.window exactly once and reader.relations at most once per returned node with {scope, to: node.key, limit: relationLimit}; never calls ingest/refresh/relate/markStale or any provider; returns a deeply frozen plain object that survives JSON round-trip losslessly.
• TimelineModel { contract; revision; topologyRevision; origin: { startedAt: string; basis: 'earliest-observed-start' } | { startedAt: null; basis: 'none' }; span: { ms: number | null; complete: boolean }; lanes: readonly TimelineLane[]; concurrency: { maxMeasured: number; basis: 'source-intervals-only'; countsOpenIntervals: true }; notes: readonly TimelineNote[]; truncated: { lanes: boolean; rows: boolean; relations: boolean; window: boolean } }.
• TimelineLane { key: string; label: string; basis: 'ownership' | 'grouping' | 'provider'; confirmed: boolean; rows: readonly TimelineRow[] }. Lane assignment per row: an incoming 'ownership' edge from a node in the same scope -> lane key = that parent's key, basis 'ownership'; else an incoming 'grouping' edge -> that parent's key, basis 'grouping'; else lane key `provider:${nativeRef.provider}`, basis 'provider'. When several parents of the chosen kind qualify, the lexicographically smallest parent key wins and note 'multiple-parents' is added; 'dependency', 'causation' and 'hypothesis' edges never assign a lane or alter timing. confirmed is true only when every edge used for the lane carries provenance.nativeConfirmationRef. Lane label is the parent's presentation.title (redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText, max 80) when the parent is inside the window, else the sanitized parent key, else the provider name.
• TimelineRow { key; nativeRef; title (sanitized, max 80); tone: Presentation['statusTone']; freshness; timing: { kind: 'closed'; startedAt; endedAt; durationMs } | { kind: 'open'; startedAt } | { kind: 'unavailable'; reason: 'no-source-interval' }; bar: { offsetCells; lengthCells; clippedLeft; clippedRight; openEnded } | null }. No field named elapsedMs, estimatedEndedAt or progressPercent exists anywhere in the model.
• Ordering: lanes by earliest row startedAt then key; rows inside a lane by startedAt then key; rows without an interval last, by key. Rows beyond maxRowsPerLane and lanes beyond maxLanes are dropped with truncated.rows / truncated.lanes true; truncated.window is total > offset + returned; truncated.relations is true when any relations page returned exactly relationLimit rows.
• Bar math: origin = earliest startedAt over rows with a parsable interval; offsetCells = floor((startedAt - origin)/1000 * zoom) - pan; closed lengthCells = max(1, floor(durationMs/1000 * zoom)); open bars extend to the right edge with openEnded true; bars are clipped to [0, columns) with clippedLeft/clippedRight flags; a bar entirely outside the viewport becomes bar null and note 'rows-outside-viewport' is added. Unparsable timestamps produce timing 'unavailable' (never a throw: the projection already validated dates).
• Concurrency: sweep over interval boundaries of the returned rows: a closed interval counts on [startedAt, endedAt), an open interval counts from startedAt to the latest known boundary; maxMeasured is the maximum simultaneous count; rows without intervals never count.
• Notes (frozen vocabulary, each at most once): 'clocks-may-differ' (present whenever intervals come from more than one nativeRef.provider), 'open-intervals-present', 'intervals-missing' (carries a count), 'stale-rows-present', 'window-partial', 'relation-page-full', 'multiple-parents', 'rows-outside-viewport', 'phase-kinds-unavailable' (always present: Interval carries no waiting/executing/blocked kinds, so lanes show source intervals only).

title: W16-B/VC-4: pure bounded workflow_observe reply builder over ObservationProjection (cursor pagination, selectors, relation and event-window metadata, last-known-running + stale freshness summary, byte cap, sanitized compact JSON); Pi tool registration excluded
description:
Gap (measured at rig HEAD ad3cf6e908f0): the registered workflow_observe tool (src/index.ts:2593-2622, hot) returns projection.query({scope, invocationId, limit}) nodes plus truncated and task fields, and furnace_observe (src/index.ts:2549-2570, hot) returns the raw FurnaceReading; neither offers a cursor, selectors, relation or event-window metadata, a freshness summary or a response byte cap, while W16 (wb-69g) names "compact bounded result and ACL" as its acceptance. docs/workbench/11 proposes workflow_observe(ref, selectors?, cursor?, limit?) returning "bounded native snapshot, event window, aggregates, freshness, anomaly evidence"; docs/workbench/09 requires Pi tool summaries to communicate "last-known-running + stale"; docs/workbench/14 lists "Pi model tool response size under bounded queries" as a benchmark measure. ObservationProjection already exposes every read needed: window({scope, invocationId, offset, limit}) -> {nodes, total, revision} (src/workbench/observation.ts:448), relations({scope, from?, to?, limit?}) (:397), events({scope, limit, ref?, after?}) -> {events, truncated, completeness} (:540), relationRevision() (:467) and stats() (:558). The ACL (grants, session/workspace/principal checks) stays in the hot tool; this bead delivers the reply shaping the tool will later call.

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free): src/workbench/observe-query.ts (new) exporting
- OBSERVE_CONTRACT = "workbench.observe/v1"; type ObserveReader = Pick<ObservationProjection, "window" | "relations" | "events" | "relationRevision" | "stats">.
- interface ObserveRequest { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId: string; cursor?: string; limit?: number (1..40, default 20); selectors?: { tone?: Presentation["statusTone"]; kind?: string; relations?: boolean; events?: { limit: number (1..40) } }; maxBytes?: number (1024..65536, default 16384) }.
- observeInvocation(reader: ObserveReader, request: ObserveRequest): ObserveReply, pure and synchronous: calls only reader methods (window once per call; relations at most once per returned node with limit <= 40 when selectors.relations; events once when selectors.events); never ingest/refresh/relate/markStale, never a provider.
- ObserveReply (frozen plain data, JSON round-trip lossless): { contract; invocationId; window: { offset; limit; returned; total; revision; nextCursor: string | null; truncated: boolean }; nodes: ObserveNode[] where ObserveNode = { key; nativeRef; kind; presentation (title and statusText passed through sanitizeWorkbenchText(value, 200) from src/workbench/redaction.ts; statusTone kept BESIDE statusText, never replacing it); freshness; completeness; sourceConnectionState; observedAt; lastConfirmedAt?; subjectBasis?; interval?; evidenceRefs (each sanitized, at most 20) ; evidenceTruncated: boolean }, never payloadRef bodies or event payloads; relations?: { perNode: { key; outgoing: Record<RelationKind, number>; partial: boolean }[]; basis: "returned-window-only" }; events?: { returned; truncated; completeness: "complete" | "partial-gap"; kinds: Record<string, number>; providers: string[] } (metadata only: no event bodies, no node presentation copies); freshness: { current; stale; unknown; lastKnownRunningStale: number; summary: string } where lastKnownRunningStale counts returned nodes with statusTone "active" and freshness !== "current" and summary contains the literal "last-known-running + stale" whenever that count is > 0, otherwise "all returned nodes current" or "N stale / M unknown"; anomalies: { disconnectedProviders: string[]; partialCompleteness: number; eventGap: boolean; noRelationsAvailable: boolean }; aggregates: "not-wired" (literal until the ancestor-aggregate read model of wb-6ze.2 is wired by a later bead; no estimated numbers); countsBasis: "returned-window"; bytes: number; truncatedForBytes: boolean }.
- Cursor: opaque base64url of JSON { v: 1; offset; invocationId }, validated on decode; a malformed, negative, non-integer, cross-invocation or oversize (> 256 bytes) cursor throws CapabilityError("validation") from src/workbench/capability-registry.ts, never a silent restart at offset 0; nextCursor is null when offset + returned >= total.
- Byte cap: the reply is measured as Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(reply)); when over maxBytes, trim in this deterministic order - events, then relations, then nodes from the tail (adjusting window.returned/truncated and nextCursor so the dropped nodes are reachable on the next page) - and set truncatedForBytes true; never drop freshness, anomalies or window fields.
- No ANSI/control characters anywhere: JSON.stringify(reply) never matches /[\u0000-\u001f\u007f‮​]/ after sanitization.

Out of scope: registering or wiring the builder into workflow_observe/furnace_observe (src/index.ts, hot); ObservationProjection changes (src/workbench/observation.ts is being edited additively by wb-6ze.2 this round; import only); aggregates (wb-6ze.2) and their wiring; control actions (wb-69g.1); inspector rendering (wb-6ze.1/wb-g1g.1); any cap change.

Files: src/workbench/observe-query.ts (new); test/workbench-observe-query.test.ts (new). Fixtures: build a real ObservationProjection with refresh/ingest/relate/disconnect as test/workbench-observation.test.ts does.
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-observe-query.test.ts fails before src/workbench/observe-query.ts exists. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

O1. Bounded pagination over the projection, never the event history. A projection holding 95 nodes under one invocationId plus 100,000 ingested updates: observeInvocation with limit 20 returns 20 nodes, window.total 95 and a nextCursor; following nextCursor yields 95 distinct keys in viewport order and then nextCursor null; a reader spy shows exactly one window() call per reply with limit <= 40 and zero events()/relations() calls when selectors are absent; a cursor from another invocationId, a malformed string, a negative offset and a 300-byte cursor each throw CapabilityError with category "validation". Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Rendering pipeline": "Pi observation tools paginate/filter/limit and return compact JSON, never rendered ANSI." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-018: "Pi can query bounded semantic observations without consuming raw event logs or terminal-rendered text."

O2. Freshness nuance is spoken, not hidden. After disconnect("furnace") on a fixture with three active furnace nodes and two success forge nodes, freshness.lastKnownRunningStale === 3 and freshness.stale === 3; every returned furnace node keeps a statusText containing its native "RUNNING" text with statusTone "active" and freshness "stale"; freshness.summary contains the literal "last-known-running + stale"; after reconnect("furnace") alone the summary is unchanged; after a refresh() snapshot for one node the count drops to 2. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Freshness and ambiguity": "A disconnected Furnace event stream must not make a previously RUNNING node permanently authoritative RUNNING; it becomes last-known-running + stale. Pi tool summaries must communicate that nuance." Quote docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md § "Observation projection": "Do not replace native status with presentation.statusTone. This is a read model only."

O3. Relations and events are metadata, with partiality labelled. With selectors.relations true, a node carrying 3 grouping, 1 ownership (with nativeConfirmationRef) and 1 hypothesis outgoing edge reports perNode outgoing { grouping: 3, ownership: 1, hypothesis: 1, dependency: 0, causation: 0 } with partial false and basis "returned-window-only"; a node with 150 outgoing edges reports partial true (relations() page limit 40, never raised); with selectors.events { limit: 10 } over 1,000 ingested events, events.returned === 10, events.truncated true, events.kinds counts by kind, events.completeness "complete", and JSON.stringify(reply.events) contains no "presentation", "payload" or title text; an after-cursor whose event was evicted yields completeness "partial-gap" and anomalies.eventGap true. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Experimental projection implementation": "Event queries expose metadata and references without raw producer payloads. Source-qualified cursor retention loss is explicitly partial-gap." Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "Missing edges do not imply independence." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-032: "Pi can use observer tools to inspect definition, retrieve bounded event windows, source/evidence refs and compare two runs."

O4. Response size is capped deterministically and honestly. With maxBytes 4096, selectors.relations and selectors.events set, and 40 nodes carrying 190-character titles: Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(reply)) <= 4096, truncatedForBytes true, events dropped before relations before nodes, window.returned === nodes.length, nextCursor points at the first dropped node so a following call returns it, and freshness/anomalies/window are always present; with maxBytes 65536 the same request fits and truncatedForBytes is false; maxBytes 512 or 1,000,000 throws CapabilityError "validation". Quote docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Input and output hardening": "Bound recursively nested JSON, bytes, array length, call count, response size and event rate." Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Performance benchmark": "Pi model tool response size under bounded queries".

O5. Nothing leaks, nothing is executable. Titles and statusText containing "\x1b[31m", U+202E, U+200B and "Authorization: Bearer abc123" come back sanitized (no control, bidi or zero-width characters; "[REDACTED]" present and "abc123" absent) at most 200 characters; evidenceRefs are capped at 20 per node with evidenceTruncated true; JSON.stringify(reply) never matches /[\u0000-\u001f\u007f‮​]/ and contains no payloadRef body; the module source (read by the test) imports nothing from node:fs, node:child_process, node:net or any provider module. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Acceptance/negative controls" item 10: "Large/secret payload does not leak into Pi tool result or screen by default." Quote docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Input and output hardening": "Treat observed tool outputs as data, not instructions for Pi designer." Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Operations telemetry": "Hide/redact prompt/tool bodies by default."

O6. Scope isolation and read-only purity. A request whose scope differs from the nodes' scope returns window.total 0 and zero nodes without any relations()/events() call; a projection spy proves observeInvocation calls only window/relations/events/relationRevision/stats (never ingest, refresh, relate, markStale, disconnect, reconnect); two calls with identical inputs on an unchanged projection are deep-equal, and Object.isFrozen holds for the reply and its arrays. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Data retention and privacy": "Tenant/workspace boundaries apply at correlation queries, not just at individual SDK calls." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-030: "Layout, reducers, status classification and control capabilities are pure/testable without a real terminal." Quote docs/workbench/03-architecture-and-ownership.md § "Design constraints": "An observation is a read, not a claim to cancel/control; explicit auth scope required for mutations."

O7. Measured counts only. countsBasis === "returned-window"; aggregates === "not-wired"; JSON.stringify(reply) contains no field named estimate, estimated, criticalPath, tokens or cost; window.total comes from window().total and window.revision from window().revision. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Aggregates and profiling": "Distinguish measured actual from estimated projected metrics." Quote docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md § "First public Pi tools (proposed)": "workflow_observe(ref,selectors?,cursor?,limit?): bounded native snapshot, event window, aggregates, freshness, anomaly evidence." and "Use compact structured schema, discover more capability detail on demand".

O8. (2) outputs through the shared sanitizers: every string is stripUnsafeText + default-ignorable REMOVAL (never space) before the keyword pass, then sanitizeWorkbenchText repeated until it is a no-op (remove-then-redact per the wb-952 ruling; converges past the wb-3l3 JSON-secret non-idempotence, pinned); bytes is measured through sanitizeWorkbenchJsonText and the reply is a fixed point of it (pinned). (3) cursor/revision semantics: cursor = base64url of canonical {v:1, offset, invocationId, scope, revision}; scope = FNV-1a tag of the workspace/principal pair (binding check, not a secret) so a cursor from another scope is refused; another invocation refused; a cursor revision above the projection's window revision is refused as out-of-order (older revisions accepted: the projection moved on); malformed/non-canonical/padded/negative/non-integer/over-256-byte cursors refused; all CapabilityError("validation"), never a silent restart. Reader rows from another scope are skipped (scanned, never returned). (4) byte cap: explicit truncatedForBytes plus droppedForBytes {events, relations, nodes}; order events -> relations -> tail nodes; nextCursor at the first dropped node; window/freshness/anomalies never dropped; worst-case skeleton measured 942 bytes (< 1024 floor).
ADDITIONS BEYOND THE BRIEF'S LITERAL SHAPES (each pinned by a test): window.scanned (cursor correctness under tone/kind selectors and byte trims of a filtered page); cursor fields scope + revision (constraint 3); relations.revision = relationRevision(); events.basis "scope-event-window" (projection events() is scope-wide and oldest-first) and selectors.events.after (the O3 evicted-after-cursor case); droppedForBytes (constraint 4); freshness.summary "no nodes returned" for an empty window instead of a vacuous "all returned nodes current"; with last-known-running the summary reads "N last-known-running + stale (active, not current); S stale / U unknown"; invocationId must be display-safe and at most 94 JSON characters so its largest cursor fits 256 bytes; unknown request/selector/cursor fields refused; reader counters JSON cannot carry -> CapabilityError("unavailable"); unknown enum values degrade to "unknown" (presentation.type to "sdk-operation", the projection's own default).
KNOWN RESIDUALS (not fixed here; redaction.ts out of scope): under remove-then-redact a control used AS the separator ("Bearer<TAB>abc") glues and the shared \s+ pattern misses it, and a word character glued before the keyword ("xBearer abc") is missed by the shared \b pattern - both belong to wb-952's probe corpus. Relation partiality assumes the projection's maxQuery >= 40 (a lower cap would cut pages undetected).

title: VC-1/W02-A: live adverse-journey tier for the Claude SDK host (mid-stream cancel after native session ID, pre-start abort, invalid model) with requested/acknowledged/terminal receipt; measurement-only, dist imports, never mocked
description:
Gap (measured at rig HEAD ad3cf6e908f0, branch workbench/implementation-program): docs/workbench/15 § "Implementation status at 2026-10-15" records VC-1 as experimental because "actual terminal operator and live adverse cancellation acceptance remain open", and the VC-1 cut requires "Ctrl-C/cancel and invalid model/permission failures behave explicitly." TRACEABILITY.md WB-010 ("Stopping the parent propagates cancellation only through established ownership and appropriate SDK API") is experimental with an empty live column. The code paths exist: src/workflow/runtime.ts RunWorkflowOptions.signal (line 323) finishes the run as { status: "killed", error: "Workflow aborted." } (line 867) after host.abortAgent(agentId) for every in-flight agent (line 853); src/workbench/claude-host.ts keeps one AbortController per agent (lines 98/156), passes it to the SDK query as abortController (line 171), aborts it in abortAgent (line 268) and returns { ok:false, skipped:true, error:"Claude SDK query was cancelled.", sessionId? } (lines 207/218/247), with onMessage/onSettled hooks (lines 42-43). Nothing exercises these against a real SDK session: qa/workbench/live-claude.mjs and live-resume.mjs prove only the happy path, test/workbench-host-contract.test.ts uses a fixture query, and forge.toml has no cancellation tier.

Scope (atomic, measurement-only, hot-file free; src/ untouched):
1. qa/workbench/live-adverse-receipt.mjs (new, pure, no src/ or dist/ import): assessAdverseJourneys(observed) -> { findings: {rule, detail}[], realised: boolean } and buildAdverseReceipt(input) -> frozen plain object { contract: "workbench.claude-adverse/v1", utc, revision, node, arch, platform, sdkVersion, model, journeys, sdkEventTypes, findings, realised, pass }. The builder throws if any string field matches /Bearer\s+\S+|sk-ant-|api[_-]?key/i or contains \x1b (redaction is the runner's job; the receipt must never carry a credential).
2. qa/workbench/live-adverse.mjs (new runner; imports ONLY ../../dist/workbench/claude-host.js, ../../dist/workflow/runtime.js, ../../dist/workbench/redaction.js and @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk getSessionInfo; cwd = argv[2] ?? process.cwd(); no vi.mock, no query override, no Pi AgentManager). One real host per journey: createClaudeWorkflowHost({cwd, model: process.env.CLAUDE_ADVERSE_MODEL ?? "claude-opus-5-5", tools: [], settingSources: [], permissionMode: "dontAsk", onMessage, onSettled}).
   J1 mid-stream cancel: the script runs parallel([agent(long prompt A), agent(long prompt B)]) where each prompt asks for about 600 words so the stream outlives the abort; an AbortController passed as the runWorkflow signal is aborted on the FIRST onMessage with type "system", subtype "init" and a session_id (fault location "after Claude SDK session ID first received"); record requestedAt. onSettled records per-agent acknowledgedAt and the host result. runWorkflow resolution records terminalAt and the outcome.
   J2 pre-start abort: the controller is aborted BEFORE runWorkflow is called; expect status "killed" and zero SDK messages.
   J3 invalid model: model "claude-adverse-not-a-model-000" (override CLAUDE_ADVERSE_INVALID_MODEL); expect a non-completed outcome with an explicit redacted error and no ok:true settled result.
3. Exit semantics (receipt printed as one JSON line and written to $CLAUDE_ADVERSE_RECEIPT when set, BEFORE exiting): 0 = realised and no findings; 1 = realised with findings (a measured violation, recorded honestly, never tuned away); 2 = not realised (gateway unreachable or unauthenticated, every J1 agent settled before the abort landed, or J3 accepted the model) with a diagnostic naming the unrealised journey. A missing or unauthenticated gateway is exit 2 with the redacted SDK error, never a skip and never a fixture substitute.
4. forge.toml: one additive [build.commands.claude-adverse-live] block (command "node qa/workbench/live-adverse.mjs", timeout 300), NOT added to the default [build] gate list (same placement as claude-live).
5. test/workbench-claude-adverse-receipt.test.ts (new vitest, offline, no network, no SDK): imports the assessor/builder from ../qa/workbench/live-adverse-receipt.mjs and runs the negative fixtures in the acceptance; also reads qa/workbench/live-adverse.mjs as text and asserts its import specifiers are exactly the allowed set above and that it contains no "vi.mock", no "query:" option and no "AgentManager".

Out of scope: editing src/workbench/claude-host.ts, src/workflow/runtime.ts or any src/ file (if J1 measures a violation, record the finding in the ledger line and the bead notes and return blocked; the fix is hot-set work); the Pi tool/TUI Ctrl-C operator journey (separate acceptance); resume-after-cancel; invalid permission-mode journeys; editing qa/workbench/live-claude.mjs; editing docs/TRACEABILITY.md.

Files: qa/workbench/live-adverse-receipt.mjs (new), qa/workbench/live-adverse.mjs (new), test/workbench-claude-adverse-receipt.test.ts (new), forge.toml (one additive block).
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-claude-adverse-receipt.test.ts fails before qa/workbench/live-adverse-receipt.mjs exists. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

J1. Cancellation is explicit, never a completion. After the abort on the first init message, outcome.status === "killed" and outcome.error === "Workflow aborted."; outcome.value is undefined; no agent in flight at requestedAt has a settled result with ok === true; every cancelled agent's settled result is { ok: false, skipped: true, error: "Claude SDK query was cancelled." } carrying the sessionId the SDK reported; agents the SDK finished BEFORE requestedAt are counted as settledBeforeCancel (reported, not a failure), and the journey is realised only if agentsCancelled >= 1, else exit 2. Quote docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md § "Tests": "No false successful tool or domain verdict after SDK result error".

J2. Three phases with their own timestamps. The receipt records requestedAt (abort call), acknowledgedAt per cancelled agent (onSettled delivering the cancellation result) and terminalAt (runWorkflow resolved), with requestedAt <= each acknowledgedAt <= terminalAt; requestToAckMs and ackToTerminalMs are measured numbers; the receipt never reports a phase it did not observe (acknowledgedAt is absent for an agent whose onSettled never fired, and the assessor then records finding "unacknowledged-agent"). Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "State/event semantics": "Cancellation request != accepted cancellation != terminal cancellation." Quote docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md § "Cancellation and steering": "Cancellation request != terminal acknowledgement."

J3. Cancellation is scoped to owned sessions and starts nothing new. After requestedAt no further SDK message of type "system"/subtype "init" is observed (initAfterAbort === 0); the number of distinct session_ids equals the number of agents started before requestedAt; every observed session_id matches /^[a-f0-9-]{36}$/ and getSessionInfo(sessionId, {dir: cwd}) returns a record whose sessionId equals it after the run (the native record exists and is neither invented nor deleted). Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-009: "Claude session IDs, input/output, tool events, native SDK failure and token usage are translated without invented values."

J4. Pre-start abort creates no native work. With the signal already aborted before runWorkflow, outcome.status === "killed", sdkMessages === 0 and sessionIds is empty. Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Fault-injection locations": "Before/after Claude SDK session ID first received; during tool execution; after output tokens streamed but before final." J5. Invalid model fails explicitly. With the invalid model, outcome.status !== "completed", outcome.error is a non-empty string passed through redactWorkbenchText (at most 400 characters, no control characters), no settled result has ok === true, and sessionIds carries only ids the SDK actually reported (possibly none); if the gateway accepts the model and completes, the journey is unrealised (exit 2, finding "invalid-model-accepted"), never a pass. Quote docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md § "Tests": "Negative: invalid model, absent credentials, malformed native output, stream error after partial text, aborted query, resumed unknown session, inaccessible cwd, invalid tool policy." Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Error and degradation policy": "Missing Claude auth -> clear config error; do not silently use Pi model."

J6. Real SDK or nothing. The runner imports only ../../dist/workbench/claude-host.js, ../../dist/workflow/runtime.js, ../../dist/workbench/redaction.js and @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk (the vitest guard asserts the import list from the file text and the absence of "vi.mock", "query:" and "AgentManager"); an unreachable or unauthenticated gateway yields exit 2 with the redacted SDK error in the receipt, never exit 0 and never a substitute. Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Test classes" C: "Integration: real Claude Agent SDK in supported test environment, actual native SDK provider version and evidence; use fixture substitutes only in tests explicitly named fixture." Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Current experimental distribution": "Missing fixture settings fail rather than skip. Their receipts establish only the surfaces actually exercised."

J7. Evidence-grade, redacted receipt. The receipt carries contract "workbench.claude-adverse/v1", utc, revision (git rev-parse HEAD or the literal "working-tree"), node, arch, platform, sdkVersion read from node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/package.json (0.3.300 at HEAD, never hardcoded), model, journeys, sdkEventTypes, findings, realised and pass; it contains no assistant text, prompt text or tool payload (only ids, types, counts, timestamps and redacted error previews), and the pure builder throws on any value matching /Bearer\s+\S+|sk-ant-|api[_-]?key/i or containing \x1b. Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Every test evidence artifact includes revision, tool versions, commands, timestamp, host, native references and actual output." Quote docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Credential boundaries": "redact tokens from logs, UI, recordings and failure messages." Quote docs/workbench/04-claude-agent-sdk-executor.md § "Streaming and progress": "Avoid printing secrets or tool payloads in overview."

J8. Offline falsifiers in test/workbench-claude-adverse-receipt.test.ts (no network, no SDK import): an agent in flight at requestedAt that settles ok:true -> finding "completed-after-cancel"; an init message after requestedAt -> finding "init-after-abort"; agentsCancelled === 0 -> realised false; a pre-start journey with sdkMessages 1 -> finding "work-before-start"; an invalid-model journey with status "completed" -> finding "invalid-model-accepted"; a receipt input containing "Authorization: Bearer abc123" -> the builder throws; a clean fixture -> pass true with every J7 field present. title: W22-B: packed npm artifact boundary falsifier (top-level allowlist, agent-tooling denylist, bundled-only node_modules, .npmignore fix for tracked .agents/ and .codex/) plus evidence-grade package-smoke receipt (revision, toolchain, host, pack determinism)
description:
Gap (measured at rig HEAD ad3cf6e908f0, branch workbench/implementation-program): `npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts --json` packs 374 files including the git-tracked agent-tooling files `.agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/beads/agents/openai.yaml`, `.codex/config.toml` and `.codex/hooks.json`. `.codex/hooks.json` wires `bd codex-hook` commands to SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PreCompact/PostCompact, so a consumer who opens the installed package directory in Codex inherits hook commands from the npm artifact. `.npmignore` already excludes `.pi`, `.claude`, `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` under its own heading "Internal contributor/agent instructions — not for distribution" but omits `.agents/` and `.codex/`. qa/workbench/package-smoke.mjs (default forge gate step `package-smoke`) denies only the `.beads/` and `.forge/` prefixes, and its receipt `{contract:"workbench.package-smoke/v1", fileCount, sha, integrity, privateStateIncluded}` records no revision, tool versions, timestamp, host or command, contrary to the docs/workbench/14 truth-label rule. Packed `node_modules/` content is today exactly the three `inBundle: true` package-lock entries (@forge/sdk 49 files, @furnace/sdk 79, @hyperunix/sdk 111); nothing asserts that.

Scope (atomic, hot-file free, no src/ edits):
1. `.npmignore`: add `.agents/` and `.codex/` under the existing "Internal contributor/agent instructions" heading. Change nothing else (qa/, docs/, examples/ keep shipping as today; see notes).
2. `qa/workbench/package-boundary.mjs` (new, plain ESM, no dependencies): export TOP_LEVEL_ALLOWLIST (LICENSE, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, package.json, forge.toml, dist, src, docs, examples, qa, vendor, node_modules), DENIED_PREFIXES (.agents/, .codex/, .pi/, .claude/, .beads/, .forge/, .furnace/, .hyperunix/, .reactive-fiber/, .github/, machines/, test/, tests/), DENIED_BASENAMES (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, biome.json, tsconfig.json), DENIED_PATTERNS (basename matches /\.jsonl$/, /^vitest\..*config\.ts$/ or /\.test\.ts$/), `classifyPackedPaths(paths, { bundledLockEntries })` returning `{ violations: {path, rule}[], topLevel: string[] }` where a `node_modules/` path is a violation unless its (scope-aware) package name is in bundledLockEntries (the package-lock `packages` entry names whose `inBundle === true`), and a pure `buildPackageReceipt(input)` that assembles the v2 receipt from already-measured values.
3. `qa/workbench/package-smoke.mjs`: keep every existing v1 assertion verbatim; add classifyPackedPaths over the pack listing (any violation fails the smoke listing every offending path and rule); pack the same tree a second time and assert identical `shasum` and `integrity`; emit receipt `contract: "workbench.package-smoke/v2"` with the v1 fields plus revision (`git rev-parse HEAD`, or the literal `unknown:not-a-git-checkout`), dirty (true/false from `git status --porcelain`, or null when revision is unknown), node (process.version), npm (`npm --version`), platform, arch, utc, command, topLevel (sorted), bundled (sorted lock entry names), denied (always [] on success).

title: W13/VC-2: Forge gate-status reader adapter projects NativeSnapshots and grouping edges (historical last_result stays unknown/partial, failed gate stays failed); tool wiring excluded
description:
Gap: the only NativeSnapshot producer in src/ is FurnaceObserver.projectionSnapshot (src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts, extended by wb-752.1); grep -rn "NativeSnapshot\|projectionSnapshot" src returns only that file and its hot consumer src/index.ts:2560. The measured native read of this workspace returned status=success with authoritative_current=false, which must appear as historical/indeterminate, never as a verified PASS.

Scope (atomic, additive, new file, hot-file free): src/workbench/forge-observer.ts exporting
- forgeGateTopology(reading: JsonValue, context: { scope: ObservationScope; target: string; capturedAt: string; observedAt: string; invocationId?: string }): { snapshots: NativeSnapshot[]; relations: ForgeObservedRelation[]; diagnostics: string[] } where ForgeObservedRelation is exactly the parameter type of ObservationProjection.relate.
- Validation: reading must be the exact provider output (contract 'forge.gate.status/v1', protocolMethod 'gate.status', source.envelope.reason_code string, source.data.packages an array of objects with a string ref of at most 256 bytes and no control characters); anything else throws CapabilityError('validation'). Unknown extra producer fields are tolerated, never required and never copied into presentation text.
- One workspace snapshot: source {provider:'forge', type:'gate-status', id:'workspace', scope: context.target}, kind 'forge.gate.status.snapshot', node.type 'sdk-operation', statusText built from source.status, envelope.verdict and envelope.reason_code (e.g. "partial · COULD_NOT_JUDGE · FORGE_GATE_INCOMPLETE · verification indeterminate"), statusTone 'unknown' unless every package is authoritative_current === true (then 'failure' if any last_result === 'failure', 'success' only if all last_result === 'success'), coverage 'partial' when source.status !== 'success' or any package is not authoritative_current, otherwise 'complete'; sourceVersion 'forge.gate.status/v1'; evidenceRefs ['forge:gate.status:<reason_code>'].
- One snapshot per package: source {provider:'forge', type:'gate-status', id: pkg.ref, scope: context.target}, statusText "<last_result> (historical; authoritative_current=false[; <unverified_reason>])" with statusTone 'unknown' whenever authoritative_current !== true; when authoritative_current === true, statusText "<last_result> (current)" with statusTone 'success' for last_result 'success', 'failure' for 'failure', 'unknown' otherwise. Never an interval (Forge gate status carries no timestamps), never subjectBasis (a target path is not a basis), never definitionDigest.
- One 'grouping' relation workspace->package per package with provenance {source:'forge-observer', observedAt: context.observedAt}; never 'ownership' (the gate.status envelope carries no native lifecycle confirmation reference, and relate() rejects ownership without one) and never 'dependency'/'causation'/'hypothesis'.
- All presentation text passes redactWorkbenchText (import from src/workbench/redaction.ts, hot — do not edit) and is bounded to 200 characters so ObservationProjection.refresh never throws on producer text.

title: W14/VC-5: Incremental ancestor aggregates over observed grouping/ownership edges in ObservationProjection (measured counts, interval envelope, incomplete-trace label; inspector wiring excluded)
description:
Gap: ObservationProjection (src/workbench/observation.ts) keeps flat per-node indexes (status, kind, basis, evidence, version, time) but no ancestor aggregate: nothing answers "how many observed children/descendants does this group or Run have, in which status tones, with which interval envelope" without re-walking relations per frame. docs/workbench/10 requires ancestor aggregates to be maintained incrementally and the overview to show "status and counts"; docs/workbench/09 § Aggregates and profiling requires measured counts with an explicit "incomplete trace" label instead of a precise critical path. wb-9x5.2 (W21-A, seat g1) explicitly deferred "adding ancestor/supernode aggregation to observation.ts or workflow-inspector.ts" to a follow-up; wb-6ze.1 (W15 nested tree) is confined to the inspector and uses no new projection API. This bead supplies the read-model half only.

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free), all inside src/workbench/observation.ts:
- export interface AncestorAggregate { key: string; revision: number; topologyRevision: number; direct: { children: number; settled: number; byTone: Record<Presentation["statusTone"], number> }; descendants: { counted: number; byTone: Record<Presentation["statusTone"], number>; stale: number; depthReached: number; truncated: boolean }; intervals: { known: number; missing: number; open: number; earliestStartedAt?: string; latestEndedAt?: string }; trace: "incomplete" | "bounded"; criticalPath: "unestablished"; basis: "observed-grouping-ownership" }
- aggregate(filter: { scope: ObservationScope; key: string }): AncestorAggregate | undefined — a copied value; undefined for unknown or cross-scope keys without any traversal.
- aggregateStats(): { adjustments: number; rebuilds: number; maxVisitedPerUpdate: number } (additive; the existing stats() shape {nodes, events, edges} is unchanged).
Child edges are outgoing relations of kind 'grouping' or 'ownership' (parent = from, child = to). Set semantics: a descendant is counted once per ancestor even through diamonds. Depth cap AGGREGATE_DEPTH = 8 (same cap as wb-6ze.1); cycles terminate at the first repeated key. 'dependency', 'causation' and 'hypothesis' edges never trigger or contribute. Hot path: a node's status/interval/freshness change (ingest, refresh, markStale, disconnect, reconnect) adjusts its ancestors by walking incoming grouping/ownership edges with a per-walk visited set — O(depth x fan-in), never a scan of nodes or events. Topology changes (relate/removeEdge of grouping/ownership edges, discard/eviction) rebuild only the affected ancestors from their bounded subtree. settled = success + failure tones; stale = descendants whose freshness !== 'current'; intervals use source intervals only (earliest startedAt, latest endedAt; an open interval increments open and never fabricates an end); trace is 'incomplete' whenever intervals.missing > 0 or descendants.truncated; criticalPath is the literal 'unestablished' (no number, no estimate, no token or cost fields).

Out of scope: rendering counts in src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts (reserved this round by wb-6ze.1 and wb-g1g.1; a later bead wires overview counts), workflow_observe tool output (src/index.ts, hot), supernode collapse, concurrency/critical-path profiling, any cap change.
Files: src/workbench/observation.ts (edit, additive); test/workbench-observation-aggregates.test.ts (new). test/workbench-observation*.test.ts, test/workbench-projection-invalidation.test.ts and test/workbench-inspector*.test.ts stay verbatim and green.
acceptance_criteria:
Red-first: test/workbench-observation-aggregates.test.ts fails before aggregate()/aggregateStats() exist. All quotes are from docs/workbench in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

A1 Brute-force equality (falsifier). A seeded deterministic fixture (no Date.now()/Math.random() in the measured path, same rules as the header of test/helpers/perf-fixtures.ts) builds >= 500 nodes with grouping and ownership edges up to depth 8 including diamonds, plus dependency/causation/hypothesis edges; after every batch of status/interval/freshness mutations and edge additions, aggregate(key) for every key deep-equals an independent brute-force recomputation over grouping/ownership reachability with set semantics. Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Rendering pipeline": "Avoid O(allHistory) collapse per frame; maintain by-node last projection and ancestor aggregates incrementally." Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened."

A2 Only observed hierarchy counts. A dependency/causation/hypothesis-only fixture yields direct.children === 0 and descendants.counted === 0 for every key; adding a 'grouping' edge changes the parent's aggregate, adding a 'hypothesis' edge between the same pair does not. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "lifecycle ownership (only if native producer confirms)", "grouping only (phase, display scope)", "inferred possible relationship (hypothesis; never treated as authoritative)". Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-037: "Source-defined edges, observed edges and inferred links are distinguishable."

A3 Incremental propagation and depth cap. On a 10-level grouping chain, flipping the leaf from active to success increments descendants.byTone.success and settled at each ancestor within 8 levels, leaves the 9th and 10th ancestors unchanged with descendants.truncated === true and depthReached === 8, and aggregateStats().maxVisitedPerUpdate <= 8 for that flip. Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-029: "Over 1000 nodes: render cost scales with visible slice and changed ancestors; no full historical-log fold per frame."

A4 Cycles and diamonds terminate. Grouping cycle A->B->A: both aggregates are finite (descendants.counted === 1 each), the test completes, depthReached <= 8; a diamond P->X, P->Y, X->Z, Y->Z counts Z once in aggregate(P) (descendants.counted === 3). Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Four views" Graph: "Cycles/unknown dynamic edges represented explicitly as \"references\" rather than rendered as a fake acyclic plan."

A5 Eviction and edge removal subtract. With maxNodes/maxEdges limits forcing FIFO eviction, discarding a counted child or evicting its grouping edge brings the ancestors' counts back to the brute-force value; stats() keeps the existing {nodes, events, edges} shape so test/workbench-observation-perf.test.ts toEqual stays green. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Derived view indexes": "Coalesce same-node repeated updates; do not rebuild entire history on each render."

A6 Measured intervals, no fabricated timing. Descendants with intervals give earliestStartedAt/latestEndedAt equal to the min startedAt / max endedAt of source intervals; a descendant with an open interval increments intervals.open and leaves latestEndedAt undefined; a descendant without an interval increments intervals.missing and sets trace 'incomplete'; criticalPath === 'unestablished' always, and JSON.stringify(aggregate) contains no numeric critical-path, token, cost or estimated field. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Aggregates and profiling": "Distinguish measured actual from estimated projected metrics. If dependencies or interval bounds are missing, suppress precise critical path claims and show \"incomplete trace\". Derive latency decomposition only with valid source intervals." Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Four views" Overview: "Critical path must be shown as *partial/estimated* when relationships/times incomplete."

A7 Freshness rollup. disconnect('furnace') raises descendants.stale to the number of non-current descendants; reconnect alone leaves it unchanged; a refresh() snapshot lowers it. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Freshness and ambiguity": "A disconnected Furnace event stream must not make a previously RUNNING node permanently authoritative RUNNING; it becomes last-known-running + stale." and "UI shows STALE/UNKNOWN visibly."

A8 Bounded work at scale. A 2,000-node, 5-level grouped tree receiving 100,000 status ingests: aggregateStats().maxVisitedPerUpdate <= 8 and aggregateStats().rebuilds does not grow with status updates (rebuilds count only topology changes); the median per-ingest time at 200 nodes vs 2,000 nodes is printed in the test output (reported, not asserted beyond the visit bound). Quote docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Rendering pipeline": "For large graphs show aggregate supernodes first." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-045: "Hierarchical agent-swarm aggregation and profile comparisons handle 10k+ nodes subject to benchmarked limits."

A9 Scope isolation. aggregate() with a key from another workspace/principal returns undefined and leaves aggregateStats() unchanged. Quote docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Data retention and privacy": "Tenant/workspace boundaries apply at correlation queries, not just at individual SDK calls."

A10 Gate: ./node_modules/.bin/biome check --write on touched files; npm run typecheck clean (no any, no inline imports); ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/workbench-observation.test.ts test/workbench-observation-perf.test.ts test/workbench-projection-invalidation.test.ts test/workbench-inspector.test.ts test/workbench-inspector-window.test.ts test/workbench-observation-aggregates.test.ts green; node qa/workbench/inspector-bench.mjs still exits 0 after npm run build; record red and green commands in the delivered ledger line; do not edit docs/TRACEABILITY.md (acceptance owner reconciles).
notes: Sr. Engineer constraint 2026-10-15: observation.ts changes keep every existing invariant green (scoped markStale, out-of-order refusal, revision semantics, cross-scope isolation, 100k/1000 benchmark) and stay bounded. Aggregates derive from observed edges only — never fabricate ownership. Base on ad3cf6e+.

Relay gate cmd_3b47cb2d8b4b PASS; Sr. Engineer independent isolated-worktree complete gate on the merge PASS cmd_5eb54b7fe4fb (lint, typing, build, test, workbench-shell, package-smoke). Surface verified as exactly the two files, observation.ts unchanged on trunk since base, no any, top-level imports, no replayedCount/WorkflowRunResult constructions.

title: W16-A: pure workflow_control decision module (grant+confirmed-ownership preconditions, observer-only and guessed-action refusal, requested/acknowledged/result receipt); Pi tool registration excluded
description:
Every `workflow_*` Pi tool and every `workbench:*` grant check lives in src/index.ts (hot, Sr. Engineer-owned), and native Furnace control would live in src/workbench/providers/furnace.ts (hot). W16's acceptance "compact bounded result and ACL" still needs a testable control core. Deliver it as ONE new source file and ONE new test file; register nothing.

src/workbench/control.ts (new), pure and provider-free:
- `interface NativeControlRequest { scope: ObservationScope; principal: { id: string; role?: string }; grants: readonly string[] | undefined; target: NativeRef; action: string; params?: JsonValue; invocationId: string; requestedAt: string }` (names follow docs/workbench/13 Host boundary `requestControl(req: NativeControlRequest): Promise<NativeControlReceipt>`; this bead implements the decision, not the host method).
- `decideControl(request, deps: { projection: ObservationProjection; now: () => string })` returns `{ decision: 'denied'; category: CapabilityErrorCategory; reason: string }` or `{ decision: 'permitted'; receipt: NativeControlReceipt }`.
- `NativeControlReceipt` phases are distinct and ordered: `requested` -> `acknowledged` -> `result`. Fields: contractVersion 'workbench.control/v1', requestId, principal, grant, policy (rule name), target, action, invocationId, ownershipConfirmationRef, requestedAt; `acknowledge(receipt, { acknowledgedAt, nativeAckRef })` and `settle(receipt, { outcome: 'completed'|'failed'|'cancelled'|'unknown'; nativeResultRef: string; settledAt })` return new frozen receipts and throw CapabilityError('validation') on out-of-order transitions or missing native references. The module never calls a provider, never mutates the projection, never fabricates acknowledged/result.

title: W12 fault gap: a non-read node() leaves no journal row until it settles (runtime.ts appends only after await callNode), so a kill after the provider side effect but before the host result, or after the result but before the append, leaves nothing for the resume tripwire and the next resume re-runs the effect live (duplicate effect); record a dispatched row before the call so a resume refuses that position as uncertain-effect until an operator reconciles it
description:
Gap (groomed by flywheel seat g2 round 5, run g2-work-r1; measured at rig origin/workbench/implementation-program e830ac2 = BOUNDARY base at groom time; anchors from git show e830ac2:<path>):

src/workflow/runtime.ts records a node() journal row only when the call settles: the live path appends at :1509 (ok true) or :1533 (ok false), both AFTER `const output = await callNode({...})` (:1482); the only pre-settlement append is the carry-forward of an already-refused entry (:1417). The admission at :1305-:1313 treats `nodeJournal.get(index) === undefined` as `{ kind: "live" }`. journal.ts:213 documents "Append one settled call. Failure to write is not failure to run." and its header promises that for any non-read effect class "the resume stops on it rather than re-running or silently replaying an effect the previous run already performed." That tripwire exists only once a row exists. Consequence: a process kill (or host crash) between the provider side effect and the host result, or between the result and the append, leaves NO row at that position, so the next resume admits the position as live and performs the effect AGAIN — the duplicate effect docs/08 forbids. docs/14 names both locations as required fault-injection points and no test exercises them (grep over test/ for "before journal append|before host result|dispatched row" returns nothing; test/workflow-effect-replay.test.ts covers only recorded rows; wb-tu1 covers a recorded row with an absent class).

Scope (atomic; W12 side-effect policy; owner ruling requested on the row shape before claim, see notes):
1. Red first, test/workflow-effect-replay.test.ts: a fixture capability with a non-read effect class and an exactly-once effect counter; the host seam throws/kills after the effect counter increments but before the result reaches the runtime (location "after provider side effect but before host result"), and a second variant settles the result but fails the append (location "after result before journal append", journal append seam injected to throw once). Today the resume re-runs the node: the counter reaches 2. Quote the counter in the red note.
2. Fix shape (proposed, owner may reshape): immediately before `await callNode` (after nodeSemaphore.acquire and the aborted/settled check) and ONLY when the current effect class is not "read" (including an absent class, mirroring wb-tu1's fail-closed reading), append a dispatched row `{ kind: "node", index, key: key ?? "", ok: false, capabilityId, effectClass (when defined), basis, dispatched: true }` through the same recordJournal seam. The settled row at the same index supersedes it on read (nodeJournal is a Map built last-wins per index, runtime.ts:719-721), so a completed run resumes exactly as today. On resume a dispatched row with no settled successor is refused at :1313 as uncertain-effect (the existing non-read refusal), the workflow_node event carries reconcile.state "pending", the hint names the producer and position, and the row is carried forward verbatim; workflow_reconcile inspect reports the position with outcome "unrecorded" (dispatched, never settled). Read-class nodes write no pre-call row: journals of read-only and agent-only workflows stay byte-identical (existing journal fixtures and assertions untouched).
3. isEntry (journal.ts:229) accepts the optional `dispatched: true` marker (anything else drops the line as mangled, as today); journal-compat.ts MIRRORS the runtime (never re-implements): a dispatched row classifies node-effectful with the dispatched marker in its census and no new class unless the owner rules one; test/workflow-journal-compat.test.ts gains the mirror case. Reconcile acknowledge/override over a dispatched row bind by entryDigest exactly as over a failed row.
4. docs/workbench/08 "Side-effect replay policy on resume" gains one sentence naming the dispatched row (owner-authored or in the same commit per the owner's ruling) and TRACEABILITY gains the row; node qa/workbench/status-ledger.mjs --strict exits 0 before delivery (12:10Z seat rule).

Open questions for the owner (recorded in notes): Q1 marker shape (`dispatched: true` vs a failure-shaped row with no marker); Q2 whether a FAILED pre-call append on a non-read node refuses the call fail-closed or keeps journal.ts's "failure to write is not failure to run" (today's policy); Q3 whether the Claude host's settled-agent prefix needs the same pre-call row for agents with non-read gates (out of scope unless ruled in).

Non-scope: no change to read replay (same effect class, basis and key, marked stale), no change to the reconcile grants (never mint reconcile:*), no change to agent prefix semantics, no change to the admission order ("Decided synchronously, before anything yields"). Required outcomes: reconciliation/uncertainty/conflict; no duplicate effects, no invented PASS, no implicit mass cancellation." -> the resume refuses the position with CapabilityError category "uncertain-effect", the workflow_node event carries reconcile.state "pending" with the producer and position, and the operator reconcile journey (inspect -> evidence -> acknowledge/override) is the only way forward, exactly as for a settled non-read row. description:
Gap (groomed by flywheel seat g1 round 4, run g2-work-r1; measured at origin/workbench/implementation-program cd5aab7; src/workbench and src/index.ts are byte-identical at the b4ca4aa tip at filing; anchors from git show cd5aab7:<path>):

docs/workbench/09 section "Aggregates and profiling" requires latency decomposition derived "only with valid source intervals" and docs/workbench/11 section "Comparative experiment protocol" requires separating "model tokens, provider waiting, Forge build time, RF context time, external queue and overlay overhead when telemetry allows". Nothing in src/workbench computes any of it: git grep -i 'decompos\|latency' over src/workbench at cd5aab7 matches only a comment (capability-registry.ts:323). The projection already carries the inputs: ObservedNode.interval {startedAt, endedAt?} (observation.ts:10, :74), nativeRef.provider (:58), presentation.statusTone (:8), freshness and sourceConnectionState (:63-65), invocationId (:70); query() pages are bounded by maxQuery (default 100, :93) and report truncated. attention.ts (wb-6ze.4) measures OPEN intervals against a caller clock and a dependency-chain critical path; timeline.ts renders lanes; neither sums or attributes closed time by provider. designer.ts compareWorkflowRuns (:217) consumes CompareRun.metrics: readonly MeasuredMetric[] (:179, :185), but the registered workflow_compare tool fills metrics: [] (src/index.ts:2554), so every comparison today reports verdict unknown for want of a measured source (docs/11 section "Experimental read-only source tools": "Missing native measured metrics yields unknown, not a claimed optimization.").

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new module src/workbench/latency.ts and ONE new test test/workbench-latency.test.ts.
- Export LATENCY_CONTRACT = "workbench.latency-decomposition/v1" (a new single-carrier literal; wb-cax.8's rule), a frozen LATENCY_CLASSES ["model", "build", "context", "queue", "query", "host", "other"] and a frozen provider map {claude-agent-sdk: model, forge: build, reactivefiber: context, furnace: queue, hyperunix: query, pi-workflow: host}; any other provider is "other" (never a guess from a title or kind).
- selectLatencyDecomposition(projection: Pick<ObservationProjection, "query">, input: {scope; invocationId; limit?: 1..100 default 100; usage?: readonly {source: NativeRef; inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number; evidenceRefs: readonly string[]}[]}) -> LatencyDecomposition {contract; basis: "observed"; invocationId; examined {nodes, truncated}; wall: {measured: true; ms; from: "root-interval"} | {measured: false; reasons}; components: one entry per class {class; providers (sorted, sanitized, bounded to 64 chars); nodes; intervals {closed, open, missing}; busyMs (sum of closed intervals); unionMs (union of closed intervals so concurrency never double-counts); measured: boolean; reasons}; waiting: {nodes; reasons: ["single-interval-per-node"]} (the projection holds one interval per node, so a waiting/executing split is unknown with that reason, never estimated); tokens: {measured: true; input; output; sources} only from supplied usage whose source matches an examined node's nativeRef, else {measured: false; reasons: ["no-native-usage"]}; overhead: {measured: true; ms} = wall minus the union of every component's closed intervals ONLY when wall is measured, examined.truncated is false and every examined interval is closed, else {measured: false; reasons}; caveat: one frozen constant stating closed source intervals only and unreconciled cross-provider clocks}. Reasons come from a frozen vocabulary (page-truncated, open-intervals, missing-intervals, no-root-interval, no-native-usage, single-interval-per-node).

title: W06/W19 defect (from the wb-6hb.4 parity falsifier): the claude-tool surface capability_invoke PERMITS a prototype-key input because zod strips a declared __proto__ key before the provider sees it, while the oracle and both node() surfaces refuse 'Prototype pollution key at invoke(...) input.__proto__.'; refuse prototype keys on the raw input BEFORE schema parsing so every surface shares one input contract (docs/06)
description: Gap (owner ruling on the wb-6hb.4 gate finding, measured at cd5aab7 with zod 4.6.7): for an input object carrying an own __proto__ (or constructor / prototype) key at any depth, the oracle in capability-registry refuses with the fixed text 'Prototype pollution key at invoke(...) input.__proto__.' and both node() surfaces refuse at the VM boundary, but the curated claude-tool surface (src/workbench/claude-capability-tools.ts) parses the raw input with a zod record schema first, which silently STRIPS the key, so the call is PERMITTED and the provider receives the stripped object. Graded Low-Medium: no authority escalation (the key never reaches the provider or the InvocationContext), but a breach of docs/06 'identical authorization and input contracts' across surfaces — a surface permitting what the oracle refuses is a widening by the falsifier's definition. Scope: scan the RAW tool input for prototype keys (own keys __proto__, constructor, prototype, at any depth, arrays included) before any zod parse, and refuse with exactly the oracle's text through the same sanitized reply path; share the scan with the registry oracle (one exported predicate, not a copy); add the cell to the wb-6hb.4 parity table and FLIP its pinned known-widening assertion in the same commit. Non-scope: no change to the oracle text or the node() surfaces. Acceptance: red test on the claude-tool surface with {__proto__: {polluted: true}} and a nested variant -> refused with the oracle text, provider never called; wb-6hb.4's pinned row flipped from 'permits (known widening wb-<this>)' to 'refuses'; full suite green; TRACEABILITY row under W19.

For large graphs show aggregate supernodes first." docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Relationships are typed and provenanced" requires "Store edge provenance with timestamp and source; Graph view styles each differently."

InspectorModel (:10-18) carries only the optional evidence read side; there is no graph model field. wb-6ze.32 (open, sequenced after wb-6ze.27 per BOUNDARY 11:13:05Z) delivers the pure model src/workbench/graph-view.ts buildGraphView(reader, {scope, focus?, viewport, caps}) and EXCLUDES "src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts and all rendering/wiring", naming "graph-branch adoption is a follow-up that joins the wb-6ze.16/.21/.23/.26 workflow-inspector.ts serialization chain". Scope (atomic, pure layout, red-first): add an optional `graph` field to InspectorModel typed from the landed graph-view exports (never re-declared here). When supplied, the graph branch of layoutInspector renders from the model only: one row per model node with provider/type/status tone; one row per typed edge with direction glyph, relation class and [provenance.source]; aggregate supernode entries rendered FIRST with their counted size; cycle and unknown-dynamic reference entries rendered as explicit 'reference' rows (never dropped, never drawn as an acyclic chain); a declared edge whose endpoint was never observed renders as a declared-dependency edge carrying an 'unobserved endpoint' marker, NEVER as unknown-dynamic (BOUNDARY 10:58:33Z rendering rule bound into wb-6ze.16: declared-vs-dynamic is the source-of-knowledge axis, observed-vs-unobserved is endpoint state); a model page flagged truncated renders a counted partial label and the footer keeps its incompleteness statement; the viewport row budget keeps the existing whole-block-or-counted-remainder rule; selection pointer, focus and filter semantics are unchanged. Every rendered string routes through the file's existing safe()/visibleWidth helpers (the shared sanitizers in src/workbench/redaction.ts). When `graph` is absent the graph branch output is byte-identical to today, so the existing graph cases in test/workbench-inspector.test.ts stay green by construction.

Excluded: dialog/host wiring that builds the model per redraw (owner's, as for wb-6ze.26/.21), src/workbench/graph-view.ts edits (wb-6ze.32 owns it; adopt its landed exports verbatim), src/workbench/topology-slice.ts, src/workbench/observation.ts, any production cap change, the hot files at groom time (src/index.ts, src/workbench/evidence-wiring.ts).

title: W16-K/VC-7 (OWNER-RESERVED): workflow_control host wiring — the Pi tool and WorkbenchHost.requestControl route one explicit native action through the landed decision core to the producer adapters (furnace stop via wb-69g.3, local-detached cancel/shutdown via wb-0kg.6, claude-agent-sdk interrupt via wb-69g.8), with the Claude host retaining the live Query per call to expose the interrupt seam; requested/acknowledged/result receipts distinct, audited and projected
description: Gap (owner, measured at a17ebb2): docs/workbench/11 § "First public Pi tools (proposed)" names workflow_control(ref, action, params?) returning requested/acknowledged/result distinct, and docs/13 § "Host boundary" declares WorkbenchHost.requestControl(req: NativeControlRequest): Promise<NativeControlReceipt>; src/workbench/control.ts is the landed pure decision core (decideControl, acknowledge, settle; NATIVE_CONTROL_ACTIONS furnace stop, claude-agent-sdk interrupt, forge cancel, plus the admitted local-detached cancel/shutdown row from wb-0kg.6), but git grep finds no workflow_control tool and no requestControl implementation in src/index.ts; the three producer adapters are pure slices (wb-69g.3 delivered, wb-0kg.6 and wb-69g.8 dispatchable) that each take an injected seam and execute only a permitted decision. Nothing wires a seam, so no operator can request a native control action through Pi. Scope (owner): (1) src/index.ts registers workflow_control behind the validated feature config, after the native loader, as the one Pi door: validates params with TypeBox, builds NativeControlRequest with host-bound scope and principal (never caller-supplied), calls decideControl against the live projection, denies render the decision core's fixed text, destructive verbs require the operator confirmation the decision core demands, a permitted receipt is executed by exactly one adapter selected by target.provider, acknowledge()/settle() record the producer's own answers, and every phase is appended to the task's control audit and ingested into the projection as an observation of the target with evidence refs to the receipt ids; (2) src/workbench/claude-host.ts retains the live Query per call (keyed by call index and the native session id once init arrives) and exposes a host-level interrupt seam { interrupt(): Promise<void> } for the wb-69g.8 adapter; the seam is dropped when the call settles; (3) adapters are called with injected seams only (furnace client, detached connection, claude query) — this slice contains no provider logic; (4) the inspector dialog's existing kill stays the runtime abort and is NOT routed through control (docs/06: no universal cancel). Blocked by wb-69g.3, wb-0kg.6, wb-69g.8. Acceptance: boot-extension journeys per producer — permitted stop/cancel/shutdown/interrupt reaches exactly its adapter with the host-bound scope and principal; a denied decision (observer-only, missing exact grant, cross-scope, unconfirmed ownership, destructive without confirmation) never reaches any adapter and renders the decision core's text; receipts appear in the projection and in the task audit with distinct requested/acknowledged/result phases and never a minted ack or result; the interrupt seam is absent before init and after settle; the Pi backend and the disabled Workbench register no workflow_control; tool description and docs/11 updated; TRACEABILITY row. Hot files when started: src/index.ts, src/workbench/claude-host.ts (announced to the fork at claim time).

title: W16-D2/VC-1: claude-agent-sdk control adapter executes only permitted workbench.control/v1 interrupt decisions through an injected session seam over the SDK's Query.interrupt() (verb imported from NATIVE_CONTROL_ACTIONS and cited to sdk.d.ts, denied decisions never reach the seam, requested->acknowledged->result echoing the SDK interrupt receipt never minted, transport success never domain verification, park-not-retry); claude-host.ts, Pi registration and live SDK excluded
description:
Gap (groomed by flywheel seat g1 round 1, run g2-work-r1; measured at origin/workbench/implementation-program b44f1ce, the BOUNDARY base at groom time; line anchors from `git show b44f1ce:<path>`; SDK anchors from the pinned @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.300, package.json:33).

The landed decision core src/workbench/control.ts lists the Claude producer's only control verb -- NATIVE_CONTROL_ACTIONS (control.ts:16-20) carries "claude-agent-sdk": ["interrupt"], and DESTRUCTIVE_CONTROL_ACTIONS (control.ts:22) includes "interrupt" -- and exports decideControl (:148), acknowledge (:186) and settle (:196) with the requested -> acknowledged -> result receipt phases (:55-70). The vendored SDK declares the matching native verb on its Query interface: sdk.d.ts:2882 `interrupt(): Promise<SDKControlInterruptResponse | undefined>` (type at :4668), documented as "only supported when streaming input/output is used" and "Older CLIs resolve to `undefined`". Nothing anywhere EXECUTES a permitted claude-agent-sdk interrupt decision: `git grep interrupt src/` finds no Workbench call site; src/workbench/claude-host.ts consumes the query as a bare AsyncIterable (ClaudeQuery at claude-host.ts:24; `for await (const message of query({ prompt, options }))` at :197) so the Query handle that owns interrupt() is never retained, and the host's abortAgent (claude-host.ts:275) is the runtime's own cancellation path (WorkflowHost.abortAgent, src/workflow/runtime.ts:205), not a workbench.control/v1 execution leg with receipts. The Furnace leg of this exact gap is wb-69g.3 (src/workbench/furnace-control.ts over an injected SDK seam) and the local-detached leg is wb-0kg.6 (ADMITTED by the owner); the Claude producer has no leg.

Spec basis: docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md § "Optional inspect/observe": "Control actions are separate, explicitly registered by a provider with per-action preconditions and acknowledgements. No mandatory universal pause/resume/cancel methods." and § "Current experimental policy surface": "No universal observe/control methods are manufactured for producers." and "An effectful invocation that loses a usable answer remains uncertain and is not retried automatically." docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Authorization design": "Control decisions require native ownership/preconditions and, for destructive actions, operator confirmation." and § "Auditability": "Record authorized principal, capability contract version, logical invocation, target native ref, reason/policy, request acknowledgment and producer outcome for control operations." docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md § "Host boundary": `requestControl(req: NativeControlRequest): Promise<NativeControlReceipt>`. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Error and degradation policy": "Expired control credentials -> deny action; preserving observation if allowed."

Scope (atomic, additive, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/claude-control.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-claude-control.test.ts. The adapter consumes a decideControl result for target.provider "claude-agent-sdk" plus an injected session seam -- an interface the adapter DEFINES and the host will later satisfy, e.g. `{ interrupt(session: NativeRef): Promise<SDKControlInterruptResponse | undefined> }`, fake in tests exactly like the injected invoke seam in src/workbench/providers/furnace.ts and the wb-69g.3 pattern. It consumes the LANDED core (decideControl/acknowledge/settle) and never bypasses or reimplements it (BOUNDARY 07:49:42Z rule, applied to Furnace and local-detached verbatim). Register and wire nothing. Do not edit src/workbench/control.ts, src/workbench/claude-host.ts (retaining the live Query per agent session is the owner's host wiring), src/index.ts (HOT), src/workbench/evidence-wiring.ts (HOT), test/workbench-control.test.ts or test/workbench-host-contract.test.ts.

Behaviour to pin red-first (mutation-proof table mutant -> red test in the delivery note):
1. Verb allowlist: the only executable verb is "interrupt", proven by importing NATIVE_CONTROL_ACTIONS["claude-agent-sdk"] (never spelling a second copy) and cited against sdk.d.ts:2882 in the delivery note (the BOUNDARY 09:16:19Z citation rule applied to this SDK); any other action for this provider is a typed refusal and the seam is never called.
2. Denied decisions (every ControlDenyPolicy, including "operator-confirmation" for the destructive interrupt and "missing-exact-grant" for a revoked control:claude-agent-sdk.interrupt grant) return a typed sanitized refusal; the seam call count is 0.
3. Permitted decision -> the seam is called exactly once with the receipt's target; the adapter never retries (park-not-retry): a seam rejection or timeout settles outcome "failed" (or stays "requested" when the rejection precedes any acknowledgment) with a redacted diagnostic category, never a second interrupt.
4. Acknowledgment echoes, never minted: a resolved SDKControlInterruptResponse becomes the acknowledged phase with nativeAckRef derived from the real receipt and the still_queued uuid COUNT (uuids themselves sanitized, never raw); an `undefined` resolution ("Older CLIs") acknowledges with a named no-receipt marker, never a fabricated uuid.
5. Transport success is never domain verification: a resolved interrupt never yields outcome "completed" or "cancelled" by itself; the result phase is settled only from an observed terminal supplied by the caller (projection), otherwise outcome "unknown" with the docs/06 uncertain wording.
6. Every string that can reach an operator (diagnostics, ack refs, refusal text) routes through the shared sanitizers in src/workbench/redaction.ts (strip, redact, strip); byte-bounded.
7. Audit: every receipt phase carries the ControlReceiptCore audit fields unchanged from the core (control.ts:40-54); the adapter adds nothing to and removes nothing from them.

Out of scope: Pi workflow_control registration (src/index.ts), host retention of the Query handle (claude-host.ts), live SDK or claude-live tier, control.ts edits, Furnace/local-detached/forge legs (wb-69g.3, wb-0kg.6).

Files: src/workbench/claude-control.ts (new), test/workbench-claude-control.test.ts (new).
acceptance_criteria:
A1 docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md § "Optional inspect/observe" ("Control actions are separate, explicitly registered by a provider with per-action preconditions and acknowledgements. No mandatory universal pause/resume/cancel methods."): the adapter executes exactly the verbs in NATIVE_CONTROL_ACTIONS["claude-agent-sdk"] imported from src/workbench/control.ts (today ["interrupt"]), each cited against the vendored sdk.d.ts declaration (Query.interrupt() at node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:2882 for 0.3.300) in the delivery note; any other action is a typed refusal with zero seam calls.
A2 docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Authorization design" ("Control decisions require native ownership/preconditions and, for destructive actions, operator confirmation."): a denied decideControl result of any ControlDenyPolicy, including operator-confirmation and missing-exact-grant, never reaches the seam (call count 0) and returns a sanitized typed refusal.
A3 docs/workbench/06 § "Current experimental policy surface" ("An effectful invocation that loses a usable answer remains uncertain and is not retried automatically."): one seam call per permitted decision; rejection or timeout is settled failed (or left requested when nothing was acknowledged) with a redacted category and is never retried.
A4 docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md § "Host boundary" (requestControl returns NativeControlReceipt): phases requested -> acknowledged -> result use the landed acknowledge/settle helpers; nativeAckRef echoes the real SDKControlInterruptResponse (still_queued count only, uuids sanitized) or a named no-receipt marker for an undefined resolution; nothing minted.
A5 Transport success is never domain verification: a resolved interrupt alone never settles completed or cancelled; result comes only from a caller-supplied observed terminal, else outcome unknown.
A6 docs/workbench/12 § "Auditability": every phase keeps the ControlReceiptCore audit fields verbatim from the core; every operator-visible string routes through src/workbench/redaction.ts sanitizers and is byte-bounded.
A7 Delivery: red-first tests in test/workbench-claude-control.test.ts, mutation-proof table, biome clean, no any, no inline imports, no existing test weakened; diff limited to the two new files; complete forge gate PASS; OWNER RULING REQUESTED in the delivery note on the per-session seam shape the host will satisfy (if declined, close as declined and nothing lands).
