title: defect(wb-g1g.2): topology slice silently undercounts remainder and labels trace observed when projection maxQuery (prod 40) is below requested relationPage (default 100)
description:
Found by flywheel adversarial review run g1-r3 of branch machine/flywheel/wb-g1g.2 (commit 54e4dcc, gate receipt cmd_87383785df8f, which carried this as finding topology-slice-silent-page-cap-undercount, CONFIRMED medium, ownerRulingNeeded).

Defect: selectLinkedTopology silently undercounts the remainder and mislabels the trace "observed" whenever the projection's own relation-page cap (ObservationLimits.maxQuery) is below the selector's requested relationPage (default 100).

Mechanism (verified in code at 54e4dcc): src/workbench/observation.ts:624-625 relations() clamps limit = Math.min(input.limit ?? maxQuery, maxQuery) and reports no truncation; src/workbench/topology-slice.ts readSide() computes full = rows.length >= page against the REQUESTED page, so a page clamped below the request is indistinguishable from a complete read. The only guard is a doc comment on TopologyCaps.relationPage ("Must not exceed the projection's own page cap") — nothing enforces it, and the DEFAULT (100) violates it for the production projection, which is constructed with maxQuery 40 (wb-6ze.27 description, measured at 24e6015: src/index.ts:2380; W21 bench qa/workbench/grouped-fixture.mjs:36 also pins 40).

Independent runtime reproduction (review worktree at 54e4dcc, real ObservationProjection, vitest): new ObservationProjection({maxQuery: 40}); 45 observed dependency edges F->n00..n44; selectLinkedTopology default caps returned downstream 10 listed, remainder {count: 30, atLeast: false}, trace {label: "observed", reasons: []}. Truth: 45 observed matching edges, so the true remainder is 35 — 5 observed edges silently dropped, the count claimed exact, and completeness claimed. Control: caps {relationPage: 40} correctly returns remainder.atLeast true and trace incomplete-trace with reasons ["relations-truncated"]. This corroborates the gate seat's probe (10 listed + remainder 30 atLeast false, trace observed, 40 of 45).

Why this refutes wb-g1g.2 acceptance: B3 "neighbors beyond caps collapse to a counted remainder, never silently dropped" and the bead title's "missing relations never fabricated, incomplete-trace labeled". A trace labeled "observed" with an exact-claimed remainder while observed matching edges are dropped is a fabricated completeness claim, reachable through the intended consumer path (wb-6ze.24 computes the slice from ObservationProjection typed relations; production maxQuery is 40).

Suggested fix (red-first): falsifier first — maxQuery-40 projection with 45 matching edges under DEFAULT caps must yield remainder.atLeast true and trace incomplete-trace/relations-truncated (or an exact count of 35). Then either (a) adopt relationsPage {relations, examined, truncated, limitApplied} once wb-6ze.27 lands (consumer adoption is explicitly excluded from wb-6ze.27's scope, so no other bead covers this) and treat truncated || limitApplied < requested as a full page, or (b) require/accept the projection's effective page cap from the caller and clamp the requested page to it. Existing behavior when the page is honored (rows.length >= page => atLeast + relations-truncated) is correct and must not regress; never weaken the delivered tests.

Every consumer therefore guesses: attention.ts:141 "relations() reports no truncation and the projection caps each page at its own maxQuery, which this selector cannot see" and re-reads pair by pair under a 2,000-read budget (:75, :155-166); timeline.ts:44 "relations() reports no truncation, so a page capped below this limit cannot be told from a complete one" and :363 flags `truncated.relations` only when `incoming.length >= relationLimit`; workflow-inspector.ts:94-98 "a projection configured below 100 truncates silently, which relations() cannot report". Same index selection as relations() (outgoing for `from`, incoming for `to`, edgesByScope otherwise), same scope-prefix guard, same exact from/to filters, same `Invalid relation query limit.` throw. `limitApplied = Math.min(input.limit ?? maxQuery, maxQuery)`. `examined` counts edges visited. `truncated` is true iff at least one further MATCHING edge exists beyond the returned rows: the walk looks one matching edge past the limit and stops. It never derives truncation from an index bucket's size, because a bucket may hold edges the exact from/to filter excludes.

title: W22-M/W06: bounded in-flight admission in CapabilityRegistry.invoke (one registry-wide maxInFlight from an exported constant, FIFO wait bounded by the existing deadline and caller signal, typed 'unavailable' admission refusal distinct from the transport deadline, provider never called for a refused request, slot held until the provider settles, never auto-retry, counts-only admission snapshot for telemetry); runtime, worker and index.ts untouched
description:
Gap (measured 2026-10-15T09:48Z against origin/workbench/implementation-program 4ca6bd5; file lines from the rig checkout, unchanged at the tip): docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md section "Runtime and host requirements" requires "Streaming bounded by max in-flight node calls, backend admission and configured quota." docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md section "Registration and resolution" requires "Establish max input/output sizes, execution deadlines, memory/event quotas and secret redaction." and its section "Current experimental policy surface" records what exists: "The host registry bounds JSON depth, bytes and wait deadlines." Measured: src/workbench/capability-registry.ts CapabilityLimits carries only maxBytes, maxDepth and deadlineMs (lines 58-65, validated at 197-203); invoke() (line 253) applies the deadline timer and the caller signal and nothing else; the only concurrency-adjacent bound anywhere is src/workflow/runtime.ts:690 `const nodeCap = 1000`, a TOTAL node-call count per workflow, so a script's parallel() over hundreds of node() calls dispatches every call at once against the native providers (forge/furnace/hx/rf CLIs and SDK clients) with no admission and no quota. Store dedupe (bd list --status all, terms in-flight/inflight/admission/quota/concurren/backpressure): no bead covers it.

Scope (atomic): src/workbench/capability-registry.ts plus one new test file. One registry-wide bound, no per-capability table (the owner can add one later); no edits to src/workflow/runtime.ts, src/workflow/worker-source.ts or src/index.ts (runtime/index.ts are HOT; the worker needs nothing because admission lives host-side where every node(), curated Claude MCP tool and Pi tool path already calls registry.invoke/inspect).

Design to implement:
- CapabilityLimits.maxInFlight?: number, validated exactly like the existing limits (safe integer >= 1, else CapabilityError("validation", "Invalid capability limit maxInFlight.")).
- One exported constant CAPABILITY_MAX_IN_FLIGHT (proposed 32) as the default; tests read the constant, never a literal (wb-oon/wb-cax.8 single-carrier precedent).
- Admission applies to invoke mode and inspect mode alike. When inFlight >= maxInFlight the call WAITS in FIFO order for a slot; the wait is bounded by the SAME deadlineMs timer and the SAME caller signal the call already has (no second clock, no new option).
- A call still queued when its deadline fires is refused with CapabilityError("unavailable", ...) whose message names admission and the bound (e.g. "Capability <id> admission exhausted: <maxInFlight> in flight after <deadlineMs>ms."); this is deliberately distinct from the existing CapabilityError("transport", "... exceeded its deadline ...") that means the provider WAS called. A call cancelled while queued keeps the existing "transport" cancellation family. In both cases provider.invoke/inspect is never called for that request.
- A slot is held until the provider promise settles, not until the caller is answered: a hung provider stays counted in inFlight after its caller's deadline rejection, so saturation is visible rather than hidden (honest backpressure; docs/06: a deadline "does not establish producer rollback").

The inputs exist: ObservationProjection exposes query() (src/workbench/observation.ts:477), events() (:540, completeness "complete" | "partial-gap") and stats() (:558 -> {nodes, events, edges}); ObservedNode carries kind, presentation.statusTone, freshness, sourceConnectionState, evidenceRefs and nativeRef (:56-76); ObservationEvent carries sourceTimestamp? and observedAt (:12-28); ingest() returns "applied" | "duplicate" | "out-of-order" (:261) but retains no counters; CapabilityErrorCategory (src/workbench/capability-registry.ts:39) names the provider outcome categories; the Claude host computes per-call token usage (src/workbench/claude-host.ts:83-89) but publishes no aggregate. wb-6ze.4 (landed a4cd2cf) set the pattern this bead follows: a pure, caller-clocked, bounded selector over one projection page with measured-vs-unknown labelling. wb-752.2 (in progress) builds the workflow_observe reply and may surface this report later; wb-cax.10 (owner-held) covers the other docs/17 residual (lazy init). Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/telemetry.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-telemetry.test.ts; wire nothing.
- export const TELEMETRY_CONTRACT = "workbench.telemetry/v1"; export const TELEMETRY_CLOCK_CAVEAT (event lag compares producer sourceTimestamp with observedAt; cross-provider clocks are not reconciled).
- export type TelemetryMetric<T> = { state: "measured"; value: T; source: "projection" | "supplied" } | { state: "unknown"; reason: "not-supplied" | "invalid-supplied" | "no-source-timestamps" | "no-events" }.
- export interface SuppliedCounters { providerCallOutcomes?: Readonly<Partial<Record<"returned" | CapabilityErrorCategory, number>>>; droppedObservations?: number; lateObservations?: number; visibleRows?: number; renderP95Ms?: number; heapUsedBytes?: number; sdkTokens?: number; claudeSessions?: number; uncertainEffects?: number } -- the host/dialog counts these (ingest results, provider outcomes, render timings, SDK usage) and passes them in; this bead defines the shape only.
- export function buildOperationsTelemetry(projection: Pick<ObservationProjection, "query" | "events" | "stats">, input: { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId?: string; now: string; limit?: number (default 100, max 100); eventLimit?: number (default 200, max 1000); supplied?: SuppliedCounters }): OperationsTelemetry -- a frozen report { contract; now; examined: { nodes; truncated; events; eventsTruncated; completeness: "complete" | "partial-gap" }; activeWorkflows: TelemetryMetric<{ active: number; lastKnownRunningStale: number }>; claudeSdkSessions: TelemetryMetric<number> (projection count of nodes with nativeRef.provider "claude-agent-sdk" and type "session"; a supplied claudeSessions is reported beside it with source "supplied", never merged); providerCallOutcomes: TelemetryMetric<Record<string, number>>; eventLag: TelemetryMetric<{ p50Ms; p95Ms; samples; unmeasured; providers: string[]; caveat: string }>; droppedObservations, lateObservations: TelemetryMetric<number>; projectionSize: TelemetryMetric<{ nodes; events; edges }>; visibleRows, renderP95Ms, heapUsedBytes, sdkTokens, uncertainEffects: TelemetryMetric<number>; nativeEvidenceCoverage: TelemetryMetric<{ withEvidence: number; examined: number }> }.
- Rules: projection-derived metrics come from ONE bounded projection.query({scope, invocationId, limit}) page and ONE bounded projection.events({scope, limit: eventLimit}) read; truncated and partial-gap flags are propagated into examined. activeWorkflows.active counts nodes with kind "workflow" and statusTone "active"; lastKnownRunningStale counts those with freshness !== "current" or sourceConnectionState "disconnected" (docs/09 § "Freshness and ambiguity" nuance). eventLag samples are observedAt minus sourceTimestamp in ms for events carrying both (negative samples clamp to 0 and are counted in unmeasured, as are events without sourceTimestamp); p50/p95 by nearest-rank over the sorted samples; providers = sorted distinct event.source.provider. Supplied metrics are measured only when the supplied value is a finite non-negative number (for the outcome record: every value finite non-negative), else unknown "not-supplied" / "invalid-supplied"; the report never defaults an absent counter to 0. now is the caller's clock (ISO-8601 with timezone; the module never calls Date.now); the projection is never mutated.
- Redaction: the report contains no node titles, status text, evidence ref strings, prompts, tool bodies or payload refs -- counts and provider names only; provider names pass redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText (src/workbench/redaction.ts) and are capped at 64 chars; JSON.stringify(report) stays under 8 KiB for the maximum page and the test asserts it.

Out of scope: host-side counting (ingest-result counters, provider outcome counters, render timings, SDK usage aggregation live in src/index.ts, the dialog and hosts -- HOT or owner wiring; this bead defines SuppliedCounters only), inspector header or workflow_observe surfacing (wb-752.2), process.memoryUsage or any node:* read inside the module, docs or TRACEABILITY edits.

Gap (measured at rig HEAD, branch workbench/implementation-program, origin 40a031a; BOUNDARY base 9bea995+): docs/workbench/16-repository-refactor.md § "Compatibility feature control" requires "Tests must run in both upstream/Pi and new/Claude workbench modes until a documented deprecation is approved", and docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Test classes" class B defines the compatibility golden as "actual upstream Claude-compatible scripts in examples/workflows plus docs/workflows.md semantics; compare stable result shape, phase grouping, parallel/pipeline ordering contract, failures, metadata, nested workflow resolution, JSON schema and budget behavior". Today every golden runs under ONE backend: test/workflow-examples.test.ts drives all five examples/workflows/*.js (compose, fan-out-audit, gated-fix, review-panel, structured-findings, plus lib/count-child.js) through runWorkflow({script, host}) with a hand-built stub WorkflowHost (stubHost(), :74-110), and test/workflow-claude-code-compat.test.ts likewise builds its own WorkflowHost (:40, :60). Nothing runs those scripts through createClaudeWorkflowHost (src/workbench/claude-host.ts:95), whose ClaudeWorkflowHostOptions.query?: ClaudeQuery (claude-host.ts:24, :41) is the injectable SDK seam; the only golden-adjacent mention of workflowAgentBackend is settings parsing (test/workbench-host-contract.test.ts:228-231). wb-a2g.2 (landed 9c1c42f) shipped test/helpers/claude-sdk-stream.ts (FakeClaudeSdk, FakeSdkCall, sdkInit, sdkAssistantText, sdkAssistantToolUse, sdkResultSuccess, sdkSuccess), which scripts deterministic SDK message streams for exactly this seam. wb-cax.4 (open) pins the registered surface per mode and wb-cax.5 (open) covers the degradation lines; neither executes the goldens under the Claude backend.

Scope (atomic, test-only, hot-file free; src/ untouched): ONE new test file test/workflow-examples-claude-backend.test.ts plus at most ONE new helper test/helpers/golden-backends.ts (a shared label->answer table so both hosts answer identically). For every examples/workflows/*.js (glob-driven, same discovery as workflow-examples.test.ts) and lib/count-child.js, run the unmodified script twice: (A) the upstream stub WorkflowHost over the answer table; (B) a host from createClaudeWorkflowHost({cwd, model: 'fixture-model', tools: [], query: fixture, ...}) whose fixture ClaudeQuery is built from test/helpers/claude-sdk-stream.ts and answers from the same table (JSON text for schema-bearing calls, prose otherwise) with a distinct fake native session id per call. Normalize both results (status; error class/message prefix; value JSON with arrays sorted only where the example's own contract is order-insensitive; agentCount / number of agent() calls; phase grouping through the existing src/workflow/progress.ts projector; metadata keys; nested resolution of lib/count-child.js; schema-rejection class; budget-exhaustion class) and assert deep equality A == B. Negative controls: (1) a spy standing in for the legacy Pi spawn path records zero calls under (B); (2) an agent() call with an unsupported option key fails at the call under BOTH backends with the same error class; (3) the SDK fixture records exactly one query per agent() call, each with a distinct session id, so a backend that batched, re-ran or skipped a call fails; (4) one deliberately divergent fixture answer makes the equivalence assertion fail (mutation proof run once, documented). No live model, no network, no TTY.

Out of scope: src/ changes of any kind (if the equivalence reveals a genuine backend divergence, file a separate bead carrying the normalized diff instead of adjusting the test or the normalizer); docs edits; test/workflow-examples.test.ts, test/workflow-claude-code-compat.test.ts and test/helpers/claude-sdk-stream.ts stay byte-identical; hot files src/ui/workflow-dialog.ts, src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts, test/workbench-security-workflow.test.ts untouched.

Specs: docs/workbench/16 (Compatibility feature control; Migration acceptance), docs/workbench/14 (Test classes B; Matrix by subsystem rows "Claude SDK host" and "Legacy scripts"; Truth labels and release gates), docs/workbench/15 (VC-1 "legacy script fixtures unchanged"; W22 "reproducible Forge gate"), docs/workbench/02 WB-003.

The HyperUnix provider (src/workbench/providers/hyperunix.ts:15-26 registerHyperUnixFind and :30-45 nativeHyperUnixFind) returns {contract:'hyperunix.find/v1', source: resultToJson(QueryResult) — representation 'hyperunix.result/1', execution_status.kind, coverage_summary.licenses_absence, rows, rows_retained, operation, coverage certificates — workspaceRoot, runtime:{version, binarySha256}} (asserted live by test/workbench-native-ecosystem.test.ts:8-11 and test/workbench-ecosystem-native.test.ts:13-21: execution_status.kind 'incomplete', licenses_absence false, no "verified":true). Nothing turns that measured read into an ObservationProjection node, so the inspector and workflow_observe never show HX coverage; TRACEABILITY WB-043 (HX cross-product provenance) is 'planned' and WB-025 ("distinguishes ... HX coverage") is fixture-only. docs/workbench/09 § "Reader adapters" names "HX: query coverage/bounds/query basis, and optional graph traversal of linked native refs"; § "Acceptance/negative controls" item 6 demands 'Native "partial" HX coverage never becomes "known empty"'; docs/workbench/07 § "HyperUnix provider": "Incomplete query cannot silently authorize 'nothing to do' or produce false success." The vendored SDK's ExecutionStatusKind is the closed set complete | complete-empty | incomplete | budget-exhausted | cancelled | view-invalidated | provider-failed | schema-failed | internal-failed | protocol-failed | usage-error | mutation-rejected | mutation-partial (node_modules/@hyperunix/sdk/dist/result.d.ts:40-68) and CoverageSummary.licensesAbsence is "True only when the runtime licensed absence" (:84).

Scope (atomic, additive, pure, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/hyperunix-observer.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-hyperunix-observer.test.ts; register and wire nothing; do not edit src/workbench/providers/hyperunix.ts (its live tests stay as they are), src/index.ts, src/workbench/designer.ts or any existing test.

• export const HYPERUNIX_OBSERVATION_CONTRACT = 'workbench.hyperunix-observation/v1'; export type HyperUnixObservedRelation = Parameters<ObservationProjection['relate']>[0]; export const HYPERUNIX_EXECUTION_KINDS = the frozen 13-member tuple above (a type-level test pins HYPERUNIX_EXECUTION_KINDS[number] to the SDK's ExecutionStatusKind).
• export interface HyperUnixTopologyContext { scope: ObservationScope; target: { kind: string; root?: string }; capturedAt: string; observedAt: string; invocationId?: string; operationRef?: NativeRef }.
• export interface HyperUnixProjectionTopology { snapshots: readonly NativeSnapshot[]; relations: readonly HyperUnixObservedRelation[]; diagnostics: readonly string[] }.
• export function hyperunixTopology(reading: JsonValue, context: HyperUnixTopologyContext): HyperUnixProjectionTopology — pure, synchronous, deterministic (timestamps come from context; no Date.now, Math.random, process or environment), deeply frozen result, JSON round-trip lossless. Imports limited to node:crypto (createHash), ./observation.js, ./capability-registry.js (CapabilityError) and ./redaction.js.
• Validation before anything else (each a CapabilityError, never a partial snapshot): contract !== 'hyperunix.find/v1' or source.representation !== 'hyperunix.result/1' -> 'validation' (unrecognized contract/representation per docs/workbench/13 § Key validations); execution_status.kind outside HYPERUNIX_EXECUTION_KINDS, non-boolean coverage_summary.licenses_absence, non-array rows, non-string operation, runtime.binarySha256 not /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/, non-string runtime.version -> 'validation'; kind 'mutation-rejected' | 'mutation-partial' -> 'validation' ("read adapter refuses mutation outcomes"); reading.workspaceRoot !== context.scope.workspace -> 'authorization' ("HX reading workspace differs from observer scope"), mirroring FurnaceObserver's identity check.
• Coverage and tone: licenses_absence true AND kind in {complete, complete-empty} -> coverage 'complete', statusTone 'success', statusText 'complete · rows N' or 'known-empty (runtime-licensed) · rows 0'; kind in {incomplete, budget-exhausted, cancelled, view-invalidated} OR licenses_absence false -> coverage 'partial', statusTone 'unknown', statusText '<kind> · rows N · absence not licensed' (a complete-empty with licenses_absence false is 'partial' plus diagnostic 'runtime did not license absence'); kind in {provider-failed, schema-failed, internal-failed, protocol-failed, usage-error} -> coverage 'unknown', statusTone 'failure', statusText '<kind>'. rows_retained === false appends ' (rows not retained)'. statusTone 'success' is never produced for partial or unknown coverage.
• Snapshot: source {provider:'hyperunix', type:'query', id: sha256 hex over canonical JSON [workspaceRoot, operation, target.kind, target.root ?? null, sorted certificate batchId strings], scope: workspaceRoot}; node {title: `HX ${operation} ${target.kind}${root ? ' ' + root : ''}` (redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText, max 120), type:'sdk-operation', statusText, statusTone}; kind 'hyperunix.query.snapshot'; coverage as above; sourceVersion runtime.version; evidenceRefs [`hx-binary:sha256:${binarySha256}`, ...`hx-coverage:${batchId}` per certificate batchId, max 32 total]; trace {invocationId} when supplied; capturedAt/observedAt from context; NO interval (the result carries no native timestamps; diagnostic 'no native interval supplied'), NO nativePayloadRef, NO subjectBasis or definitionDigest (not supplied by the read); diagnostics always include 'query id is a derived digest, not a native identifier'.
• Relations: when context.operationRef is supplied, exactly one {scope, from: operationRef, to: snapshot.source, kind:'grouping', provenance:{source:'hyperunix', observedAt}} with NO nativeConfirmationRef (display grouping only); otherwise none. Never 'ownership', 'causation', 'dependency' or 'hypothesis'.
• Row bodies, claim payloads and certificate bodies never appear in any output field; diagnostics are sanitized and capped at 8 entries of <= 200 characters.

2. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Acceptance/negative controls" item 6: 'Native "partial" HX coverage never becomes "known empty".' and docs/workbench/07-native-integrations.md § "HyperUnix provider": "Incomplete query cannot silently authorize 'nothing to do' or produce false success." -> rows [] with kind 'incomplete' and licenses_absence false -> coverage 'partial', tone 'unknown', statusText containing 'absence not licensed' and never 'known-empty'; kind 'complete-empty' with licenses_absence true -> coverage 'complete', statusText 'known-empty (runtime-licensed) · rows 0'; kind 'complete-empty' with licenses_absence false -> coverage 'partial' plus diagnostic 'runtime did not license absence'; kinds 'budget-exhausted', 'cancelled', 'view-invalidated' -> coverage 'partial', tone 'unknown'; each failure kind -> coverage 'unknown', tone 'failure'; a table-driven test over all 13 kinds x both licence values shows JSON.stringify(result) never contains '"verified"' and statusTone 'success' appears only for complete coverage.
3. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Experimental projection implementation": "Native keys include provider, type, scope and identifier." and § "Acceptance/negative controls" item 4: "Two native sources reuse an identifier; provider-qualified keys do not collide." -> two readings with identical operation/target in different workspaceRoots (each context.scope.workspace equal to its own root) produce different source.id and source.scope; a furnace NativeSnapshot whose id string equals the HX source.id coexists in one projection (stats().nodes === 2); the derived-id diagnostic is present; identical inputs produce identical ids on repeated calls.
4. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Relationships are typed and provenanced": "grouping only (phase, display scope)" and "lifecycle ownership (only if native producer confirms)" -> with operationRef exactly one relation of kind 'grouping' from operationRef to the snapshot source with provenance.source 'hyperunix' and no nativeConfirmationRef; without operationRef zero relations; the set of emitted kinds over every fixture is a subset of {'grouping'}; expectTypeOf<HyperUnixObservedRelation>().toEqualTypeOf<Parameters<ObservationProjection['relate']>[0]>().
5. docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md § "Key validations": "unrecognized SDK message version => diagnostic rather than silent success" and docs/workbench/07-native-integrations.md § "Shared integration requirements": "Every live adapter records: SDK package + revision, native operation IDs, owner/basis, observed evidence, error taxonomy" -> contract 'hyperunix.find/v2', representation 'hyperunix.result/2', kind 'done', licenses_absence 'false' (a string), binarySha256 'abc' and a missing runtime.version each throw CapabilityError with category 'validation' and produce no snapshot; workspaceRoot '/other' against scope.workspace '/ws' throws 'authorization'; 'mutation-rejected' and 'mutation-partial' throw 'validation' with a message containing 'mutation'; a type-level test pins HYPERUNIX_EXECUTION_KINDS[number] to the SDK's ExecutionStatusKind so an SDK enum change fails typing.
6. docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Input and output hardening": "Validate Unicode and terminal escape sequences before display (no untrusted ANSI injection)." and docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Acceptance/negative controls" item 10: "Large/secret payload does not leak into Pi tool result or screen by default." -> operation 'find\x1b[31m', target.kind 'hx.fs/‮regular' and root 'src Bearer abc123' appear in node.title and diagnostics with escape/bidi characters removed and the credential replaced by the redaction marker, title <= 120 characters; a row body {path:'SECRET-ROW-BODY'} and a certificate body 'SECRET-CERT' never appear in JSON.stringify(result); 40 certificates yield at most 32 evidenceRefs.
7. docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Rendering pipeline": "Pure layout and keyboard reducers are unit-tested without a TTY." (applied to this pure adapter) -> every test runs without an HX binary, TTY or network (the live hyperunix tests are untouched and remain the only live evidence); results are deeply frozen and JSON round-trip lossless; the module source (read by the test) contains none of 'Date.now', 'Math.random', 'process.', 'child_process', 'node:fs', 'import(' and imports only node:crypto, ./observation.js, ./capability-registry.js and ./redaction.js.

title: W15-E/VC-5: bounded Furnace Attempt log evidence reader for the docs/20 "furnace run" EvidenceLoader row (run/attempt/stream identity checks, attempt of another run is unauthorized, lossy/incomplete/paged reads load with truncated true, sanitized bounded preview lines, no raw payload retained, zero control verbs); EvidenceLoader wrapper and wiring excluded
description:
Gap (measured at rig HEAD 1fc74f0, branch workbench/implementation-program): docs/workbench/20-evidence-loader-contract.md § "Producer mapping" binds the furnace row — ref "native Attempt id listed on the owning run node", resolution "the observer's bounded logs read with its run/attempt/stream identity checks; lossy, incomplete or paged reads are loaded with truncated true; an attempt belonging to another run is unauthorized", grant furnace:inspect — but nothing in src/ performs that read as evidence: FurnaceObserver.snapshot (src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts:83-125) reads only the LAST attempt's stdout as a 512-byte FurnaceLogReference {attemptId, stream, complete, lossy, returned, nextCursor} for the reading, never for an operator-selected attempt or stderr, and discards the lines; the inspector details view prints evidenceRefs strings only ('Evidence / details · producer references, not fetched payload', src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts:192). wb-g1g.1 (ready, dispatch-held) delivers the contract module src/workbench/evidence-loader.ts and the inspector slice; docs/20 § "Types" rules that loaders route provider-first and that "every preview line passes the shared redaction and terminal sanitizers plus a loader-local zero-width strip; raw payloads are never retained". The native surface already exists and is typed by FurnaceObserverClient.logs.read(id, {attempt, limit, stream:'stdout'|'stderr'}, {timeoutMs}) -> Response<LogsReadDto> {kind:'logs_read', requestId, data:{run_id, attempt_id, stream, complete, lossy, returned, next_cursor, lines}} (furnace-observer.ts:10-14 and :99-107).

Scope (atomic, I/O only through the injected client, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/furnace-evidence.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-furnace-evidence.test.ts; register and wire nothing; do not edit src/workbench/furnace-observer.ts, src/workbench/evidence-loader.ts (does not exist yet; wb-g1g.1), src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts, src/index.ts or src/workbench/designer.ts.

• export const FURNACE_EVIDENCE_CONTRACT = 'workbench.furnace-evidence/v1'.
• export interface FurnaceEvidenceRequest { client: Pick<FurnaceObserverClient,'logs'>; runId: string (/^frn-run-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,100}$/); workspaceRoot: string; owningRunNode: { nativeRef: NativeRef; evidenceRefs: readonly string[] } (the projection node the ref was listed on); attemptId: string (/^frn-atm-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,100}$/); stream: 'stdout' | 'stderr'; maxBytes: number (1..65536); maxLines: number (1..200); timeoutMs: number (1..2147483647); signal: AbortSignal; capturedAt: () => string (injected clock; the module never calls Date.now) }.
• export interface FurnaceEvidenceContent { contract: typeof FURNACE_EVIDENCE_CONTRACT; kind: 'furnace.attempt.log'; provider: 'furnace'; nativeRef: NativeRef ({provider:'furnace', type:'attempt', id: attemptId, scope: workspaceRoot}); stream; capturedAt; bytes: number (the producer's returned count); truncated: boolean (lossy || !complete || next_cursor !== null || lines dropped by maxLines); preview: readonly string[] (each line through redactWorkbenchText then stripUnsafeText then a local zero-width strip of U+200B-U+200D, U+2060 and U+FEFF, max 200 characters, at most maxLines lines, plus a final '… truncated (producer: lossy|incomplete|paged|budget)' line whenever truncated); producerReceipt: { requestId: string; complete: boolean; lossy: boolean; nextCursor: string | null }; freshness: 'current' } — the docs/20 EvidenceContent shape minus store-level fields, so the furnace EvidenceLoader of the wb-g1g.1 follow-up returns it after applying the owning node's freshness.
• export async function readFurnaceAttemptLogEvidence(request: FurnaceEvidenceRequest): Promise<FurnaceEvidenceContent> — preconditions before any client call (each a CapabilityError, no read performed): owningRunNode.nativeRef must equal {provider:'furnace', type:'run', id: runId, scope: workspaceRoot} else 'authorization' ("evidence ref is not listed on a furnace run node of this scope"); attemptId must appear in owningRunNode.evidenceRefs else 'authorization' (an attempt belonging to another run is unauthorized, docs/20); invalid ids, stream or budgets -> 'validation'; signal already aborted -> 'transport' ("Furnace evidence read cancelled before launch"). Exactly one client.logs.read(runId, {attempt: attemptId, limit: maxBytes, stream}, {timeoutMs}) call, raced against request.signal (abort -> 'transport'; the SDK promise is abandoned, never awaited further). Response validation mirrors furnace-observer.ts:101-104: response.kind !== 'logs_read' -> 'unavailable' ("response kind differs from requested native read"); data.run_id !== runId || data.attempt_id !== attemptId || data.stream !== stream -> 'authorization' (identity drift); non-array lines, non-integer returned, returned < 0 or returned > maxBytes, non-boolean complete/lossy, next_cursor not string|null -> 'unavailable' ("malformed native log shape"). Thrown SDK errors are rethrown as CapabilityError('unavailable', preview) where preview is the message through redactWorkbenchText capped at 200 characters, never verbatim.
• No control verb exists on the accepted client type (Pick<FurnaceObserverClient,'logs'>) and a runtime spy proof asserts runs.get/stop/pause/resume and work.retry are never called even when present on the injected object.

Files: src/workbench/furnace-evidence.ts (new), test/workbench-furnace-evidence.test.ts (new). Specs: docs/workbench/20 (Types; Producer mapping; Refusal and freshness rules), docs/workbench/09 (Data retention and privacy; Acceptance/negative controls 8 and 10), docs/workbench/10 (Four views — Details; Failure and deception defenses; Rendering pipeline), docs/workbench/12 (Input and output hardening), docs/workbench/08 (Cancellation and ownership), docs/workbench/13 (Key validations).
acceptance_criteria:
All criteria quote docs/workbench specs in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program, HEAD 1fc74f0 or later; docs/workbench/20 rules where older bead text disagrees).

1. docs/workbench/20-evidence-loader-contract.md § "Producer mapping" (furnace run): "the observer's bounded logs read with its run/attempt/stream identity checks; lossy, incomplete or paged reads are loaded with truncated true; an attempt belonging to another run is unauthorized" -> with a vi.fn client returning {kind:'logs_read', requestId:'req-logs', data:{run_id, attempt_id, stream:'stderr', complete:true, lossy:false, returned:120, next_cursor:null, lines:[...]}} the content has kind 'furnace.attempt.log', nativeRef {provider:'furnace', type:'attempt', id: attemptId, scope: workspaceRoot}, stream 'stderr', bytes 120, truncated false and producerReceipt.requestId 'req-logs'; each of lossy:true, complete:false, next_cursor:'c2' and 300 lines with maxLines 200 yields truncated true with the matching reason word in the final preview line; an attemptId absent from owningRunNode.evidenceRefs, or an owning node of another run or workspace, rejects with CapabilityError category 'authorization' and client.logs.read is never called.
2. docs/workbench/20-evidence-loader-contract.md § "Types": "every preview line passes the shared redaction and terminal sanitizers plus a loader-local zero-width strip; raw payloads are never retained" and docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Data retention and privacy": "Avoid raw prompts/tool bodies by default; store reference/short redacted preview" -> lines containing 'Authorization: Bearer abc123', '\x1b[31m', U+202E, U+200B and U+FEFF render with the redaction marker and without escape, bidi or zero-width characters, each <= 200 characters; for a line 'SECRET-LINE Bearer abc123' the string 'abc123' appears zero times in JSON.stringify(content) and no key named lines, raw, data or payload exists on the content.
3. docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Acceptance/negative controls" item 8: "Closing observer causes zero cancellation calls." and docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Cancellation and ownership": "Child cancellation depends on explicit native owner rights and native API semantics." -> an injected client that also carries runs.get(...).stop/pause/resume and work.retry spies sees none of them called across every fixture including abort; aborting request.signal while logs.read is pending rejects with 'transport' and the content promise never resolves; a pre-aborted signal rejects before logs.read is called (spy count 0).
4. docs/workbench/20-evidence-loader-contract.md § "Refusal and freshness rules": "Transport success never implies verification." and docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Failure and deception defenses": "Node result with missing evidence is not marked verified merely because process exited 0." -> the content has no verified, status, tone or outcome field and freshness is the literal 'current' (the owning node's freshness is applied by the loader/store per docs/20, not here); JSON.stringify(content) never contains '"verified"'.
5. docs/workbench/13-contracts-and-config.md § "Key validations": "unrecognized SDK message version => diagnostic rather than silent success" -> response kind 'run_status' -> 'unavailable'; data.run_id, attempt_id or stream differing from the request -> 'authorization'; returned 70000 against maxBytes 65536, lines 'x' (non-array) and lossy 'no' each -> 'unavailable'; a thrown SDK Error('ENOENT /home/alice/.furnace Bearer zzz') surfaces as CapabilityError('unavailable') whose message carries the redaction marker, lacks 'zzz' and is <= 200 characters.
6. docs/workbench/10-terminal-inspector.md § "Four views" (Details): "Large content loaded only on focus." and § "Rendering pipeline": "Pure layout and keyboard reducers are unit-tested without a TTY." -> the module performs exactly one logs.read per call (spy), never lists attempts or reads run status; the module source (read by the test) imports only ./furnace-observer.js (types), ./observation.js (types), ./capability-registry.js and ./redaction.js and contains none of 'node:', 'process.', 'Date.now', 'Math.random', 'import('; capturedAt comes from request.capturedAt; every test runs without a Furnace binary, TTY or network.

title: W21-B: observation recovery and bounded-query size benchmark receipt (ingest events/s, retained memory, disconnect -> stale -> reconnect-alone falsifier -> per-snapshot reconcile latency, evicted-cursor partial-gap detection, query/window/relations/events byte sizes) at 1k/100k default limits and 10k/100k bench-only limits; measurement-only, src untouched
description:
Gap (measured at rig 1fc74f0): docs/workbench/14 § "Performance benchmark" lists metrics no bench records: "observer ingest events/s and projection memory", "recover snapshot/cursor latency" and "Pi model tool response size under bounded queries". qa/workbench/inspector-bench.mjs (receipts cmd_9572ac580306, cmd_4ff4ffabcbe0) measures navigation only; wb-9x5.1 (W21, ready) measures grouped navigation/layout/terminal bytes; test/workbench-observation-perf.test.ts:11 asserts one query's examined count (<4) and bytes (<2000) with no receipt and no recovery; test/workbench-observation.test.ts:43 proves "reconnect alone cannot restore current without snapshot" at toy scale only. The recovery API exists in src/workbench/observation.ts: disconnect():356, reconnect():369, refresh():318, markStale():344, events():540 (completeness "complete" | "partial-gap"), query():477, window():448, relations():397, stats():558, MAX_DEFAULT:93 {maxEvents 20000, maxNodes 2000, maxEdges 4000, maxPayloadBytes 4096, maxQuery 100}. furnace_observe (src/index.ts:2555-2563) polls once (maxPolls 1) and relies on projection.refresh/markStale for freshness, so recovery cost at scale is an unmeasured VC-4/VC-5 claim.

Scope (atomic, measurement-only, hot-file free; no production limit or behavior change):
• qa/workbench/observation-recovery-receipt.mjs (new, pure, no src/ or dist/ import): buildFixture({seed, nodes, events, providers}) -> plain data {snapshots: NativeSnapshot[], updates: ObservationEvent[], shape} (deterministic: no Date.now or Math.random in the measured path, timestamps derived from one fixed epoch, same rules as the header of test/helpers/perf-fixtures.ts; provider mix forge/furnace/claude-agent-sdk; one invocationId and one scope); measureRecovery(ProjectionClass, fixture, {limits?, provider, queryLimit}) -> measurement (exported so vitest passes the src class and the CLI passes the dist class); assessRecovery(measurement) -> {findings: {rule, detail}[], realised: boolean}; buildReceipt(input) -> frozen plain object {contract: "workbench.observation-recovery/v1", utc, revision, node, arch, platform, cpus, passes, findings, realised, pass}.

title: W14/VC-5-C: pure attention and bottleneck selector over ObservationProjection (waiting/stale/unknown/disconnected counts, top measured open intervals from source intervals, dependency-chain critical path only as partial-estimated else incomplete-trace with reasons; caller clock, bounded, sanitized); inspector and tool wiring excluded
description:
Gap (measured at rig 1fc74f0): docs/workbench/10 § "Four views" (Overview) requires "status and counts, compact nested tree, active operations, attention panel and top measured bottlenecks" with the critical path "shown as *partial/estimated* when relationships/times incomplete", and docs/workbench/09 § "Aggregates and profiling" requires measured-vs-estimated separation with "incomplete trace" whenever intervals or dependencies are missing. Today src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts:156-157 prints two CONSTANT strings regardless of data ('Attention: stale/unknown is last-known state, not live progress.' and 'Critical path: incomplete trace (no complete dependency/interval proof).'), pinned by test/workbench-inspector.test.ts:112-116 and :195-198. Nothing in src/ computes attention items, bottlenecks or a dependency-chain estimate from observed data: grep -rn 'bottleneck\|criticalPath' src returns only designer.ts:183/236 (criticalPath "unestablished" for run comparisons; hot, untouched) and the inspector constants. wb-6ze.2 (ancestor aggregates in observation.ts) pins criticalPath 'unestablished' and lists "concurrency/critical-path profiling" out of scope; wb-6ze.1 owns the inspector file this run; wb-752.2 builds the workflow_observe reply. This bead supplies the pure selector both consumers wire later.

Scope (atomic, additive, new file, hot-file free): src/workbench/attention.ts exporting
• ATTENTION_CONTRACT = "workbench.attention/v1".
• selectAttention(projection: Pick<ObservationProjection, "query" | "relations">, input: { scope: ObservationScope; invocationId: string; now: string; limit?: number; bottlenecks?: number }): AttentionReport.
• AttentionReport = { contract: typeof ATTENTION_CONTRACT; basis: "observed"; now: string; examined: { nodes: number; truncated: boolean }; counts: { active; waiting; success; failure; unknown; stale; disconnected; withInterval; withoutInterval }; disconnectedProviders: string[]; bottlenecks: { key; nativeRef; title; tone; freshness; openMs: number; measured: true }[]; unmeasured: number; clockSkew: number; criticalPath: { label: "incomplete-trace"; reasons: ("no-dependency-edges" | "missing-intervals" | "open-intervals" | "hypothesis-edges" | "cycle" | "truncated")[] } | { label: "partial-estimated"; keys: string[]; measuredMs: number; coverage: { chainNodes: number; dependencyEdges: number }; caveat: string }; clockCaveat: string }.
• Rules. `now` is the CALLER's clock (ISO-8601 with timezone; the module never calls Date.now()). Nodes come from ONE bounded projection.query({scope, invocationId, limit: input.limit ?? 100}) call; examined.truncated propagates its truncated flag. openMs = now − interval.startedAt for nodes with statusTone 'active' or 'waiting' that have interval.startedAt and no endedAt; a producer startedAt later than now clamps openMs to 0 and increments clockSkew; nodes without an interval are counted in unmeasured and never ranked; ranking is openMs descending then key ascending (deterministic); bottlenecks.length <= input.bottlenecks ?? 5 and every entry carries measured: true. counts.stale = nodes with freshness !== 'current'; counts.disconnected = nodes with sourceConnectionState 'disconnected'; disconnectedProviders = sorted distinct nativeRef.provider of those nodes. Tones are counted separately (waiting is never folded into active or stale).
• criticalPath. Dependency edges come from projection.relations({scope, from: key, limit}) for examined keys only, kind 'dependency' only. 'partial-estimated' requires ALL of: at least one dependency edge among examined nodes; no 'hypothesis' edge among examined nodes; no cycle on dependency edges; query not truncated; every node on the chosen chain has a COMPLETE interval (startedAt and endedAt). measuredMs is the sum of complete interval durations along the longest-duration dependency chain (DAG longest path); keys lists that chain in dependency order; the caveat literal is "Observed dependency edges and complete source intervals only; missing edges do not imply independence." Anything else returns incomplete-trace carrying EVERY applicable reason. The label is never "exact" or "complete" and no number is emitted without the partial-estimated label.
• clockCaveat literal: "openMs uses the caller clock against producer startedAt; cross-provider clocks are not reconciled."
• Every title passes redactWorkbenchText (import from src/workbench/redaction.ts; do not edit) and is cut to 120 characters; control characters never survive; JSON.stringify(report).length < 16384 at limit 100 / bottlenecks 5.

Out of scope: rendering in src/ui/workflow-inspector.ts (wb-6ze.1 / wb-g1g.1 territory this run), the workflow_observe reply (wb-752.2) and src/index.ts, any edit to src/workbench/observation.ts (wb-6ze.2 owns the aggregate API; this bead only CALLS query/relations), token/cost/retry metrics (no producer supplies them), designer.ts (hot).

description:
Gap: docs/workbench/15 names "native immutable deployment refs" as VC-7 acceptance and docs/workbench/08 says native executable identity is an unestablished release obligation; W18 (wb-5w0) notes "Native binaries ... not claimed" and W22 (wb-cax) notes "Full release/install native binary identity ... remain open". At rig ad3cf6e the detached host hard-codes `nativeRuntimeIdentity: "unsupported"` (src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts:82 and :96) and its runtimeClosure comment reads "Native executables launched by SDK defaults/PATH still have unsupported identity."; src/workbench/providers/forge.ts:80 launches ServerConnection.spawn("forge"), a bare PATH-resolved name; the Claude Agent SDK's Options.pathToClaudeCodeExecutable (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:1984) "Uses the built-in executable if not specified." Nothing in src/ can observe, pin or compare the bytes of a native executable, so no host can honestly report which binary it launched or refuse reattachment when that binary changed.

Scope (atomic, pure, hot-file free): ONE new source file src/workbench/executable-identity.ts and ONE new test file test/workbench-executable-identity.test.ts; wire nothing.
- export const EXECUTABLE_IDENTITY_CONTRACT = 'workbench.executable-identity/v1'
- export type ExecutableIdentityReason = 'sdk-default-executable' | 'not-found' | 'not-a-file' | 'not-executable' | 'symlink-depth' | 'too-large' | 'unreadable' | 'path-resolved' | 'shadowed-candidates' | 'search-truncated' (frozen set; nothing else is ever emitted).
- export interface ExecutableObservation { contractVersion: typeof EXECUTABLE_IDENTITY_CONTRACT; requested: string | undefined; resolution: 'absolute' | 'path-search' | 'unresolved'; resolvedPath?: string; realPath?: string; symlinkHops: number; digest?: string (sha256:<hex>); sizeBytes?: number; mode?: number; candidates: number; immutability: 'digest-observed' | 'mutable-path' | 'unsupported'; reasons: readonly ExecutableIdentityReason[]; observedAt: string }
- export function observeExecutableIdentity(input: { command: string | undefined; cwd: string; path: string | undefined; observedAt: string; maxBytes?: number; maxSearchEntries?: number; maxSymlinkHops?: number }): ExecutableObservation — synchronous; reads only through node:fs (lstat, readlink, stat, chunked reads for hashing — never readFileSync of a whole binary); never imports node:child_process; never reads process.env (PATH is an explicit input); never throws for a missing, unreadable, non-regular, non-executable or oversized target — those are 'unresolved'/'unsupported' with a reason.
  • command undefined or empty -> resolution 'unresolved', immutability 'unsupported', reasons ['sdk-default-executable'] (the honest answer for the Claude built-in executable and any SDK default).
  • command containing a path separator -> resolved against cwd; symlinks followed hop by hop (count hops; above maxSymlinkHops, default 16, -> 'unsupported' with 'symlink-depth'); must be a regular file with an execute bit; hashed with sha256 when sizeBytes <= maxBytes (default 512 MiB) -> resolution 'absolute', immutability 'digest-observed'; oversize -> digest omitted, immutability 'unsupported', reasons ['too-large'].
  • bare command -> PATH searched in order (split on path.delimiter; at most maxSearchEntries, default 64, further entries ignored and 'search-truncated' recorded; relative or empty entries resolved against cwd); the first regular executable file wins; candidates counts every searched entry holding a same-named executable; resolution 'path-search'; the digest IS observed but immutability is 'mutable-path' with reasons ['path-resolved'] plus 'shadowed-candidates' when candidates > 1. A digest never upgrades a PATH-resolved binary to 'digest-observed'.
  • Result and its reasons are frozen; resolvedPath and realPath pass through redactWorkbenchText (paths may embed tokens); absent fields mean not observed, never a default.
- export function compareExecutableIdentity(recorded: ExecutableObservation, current: ExecutableObservation): { verdict: 'same' | 'changed' | 'unknown'; differences: readonly string[] } — 'same' only when both digests are present and equal AND both immutability values are 'digest-observed'; 'changed' when both digests are present and differ; otherwise 'unknown' (a mutable-path or unsupported side can never yield 'same'); differences names each differing field (digest, realPath, sizeBytes, mode, immutability, resolution).

Out of scope: editing src/workbench/hosts/local-detached.ts (in flight under wb-6hb.1; the 'unsupported' literal is W18's later wiring point), src/workbench/providers/forge.ts, src/workbench/claude-host.ts, src/workbench/identity.ts; discovering the Claude built-in executable path from SDK internals; remote host authentication; Furnace ExecutorApp. If acceptance cannot be met without touching a hot or reserved file, stop and return blocked.

D1. An effect that happened is never repeated and never reported as a verdict. In F1 the marker count for "effect-crash" is exactly 1 after the crash, after inspect() reports terminal "unknown" (observation "unknown", source "local-client-transport", reconcileHint matching /never.*retry|do not.*retry/i, no result field), after execute() rejected and after the same-id relaunch rejected /exists|conflict/; the snapshot never reports terminal "completed" or "failed" for that invocation. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Adversarial test matrix": "Kill after Furnace side effect before returned Run ID; kill after workspace edit before recorded result; ... Required outcomes: reconciliation/uncertainty/conflict; no duplicate effects, no invented PASS, no implicit mass cancellation." Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Optional local detached profile": "Inspection after host loss reports unknown with producer reconciliation guidance; it does not replay a saved terminal verdict or rerun JavaScript." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-026: "Interrupted effectful operation is reconciled through producer or marked uncertain; no automatic blind repeat."

D2. A lost result is not evidence the effect did not happen. The F1 receipt records effectObserved true (the marker exists) together with terminal "unknown", and the assessor records finding "effect-denied" if any journey field claims the effect did not occur. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "State/event semantics": "An observed timeout or disconnect is *not* evidence that side effect never happened." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md § "Nonfunctional invariants" NFR-02: "No host auto-retry of ambiguous irreversible writes."

D3. A deliberate second request is a new logical invocation, not a retry. "effect-crash-second" is accepted, writes exactly one marker of its own, and the receipt labels it explicitSecondRequest true with totalMarkers 2 across two ids; a relaunch under the ORIGINAL id stays refused. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Separate four identities": "Logical invocation: caller-created unique identity stable across retry of same request; distinct from identical intentional second request." Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Runtime and host requirements": "A Pi UI reconnect is only an observer/client action; it must not restart external work."

D4. Cancellation has three phases and touches one host. In F2 cancel() returns { accepted: true, terminalConfirmed: false }; the next inspect() of "iso-a" shows cancellationRequested true before terminal "cancelled" appears; "iso-b" keeps observation "observed-running" or "observed-started", terminal undefined, cancellationRequested false and controlAudit [] throughout, and ends only by its own shutdown command. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "State/event semantics": "Cancellation request != accepted cancellation != terminal cancellation." Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Cancellation and ownership": "Multi-reader shared child MUST NOT be stopped merely because one reader closed Pi or stopped waiting." Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Fault-injection locations": "Concurrent readers with one shared child; stopping one reader must not stop child without ownership."

D5. Shutdown reports unresolved effects honestly. In F3 shutdown of the running "unresolved" host returns unresolvedEffects true and of the never-executed "idle" host returns unresolvedEffects false; the later inspect() of "unresolved" is terminal "unknown" with a reconcileHint, never "completed". Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Runtime and host requirements": "Shutdown: stop accepting calls, notify owned local tasks, attempt graceful end, report unresolved effects, and release owned resources." Quote docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-041: "Optional detached workbench host permits Pi client disconnect/reconnect, without falsely claiming crash durability."

D6. SIGTERM is loss, not completion. In F4 inspect() after SIGTERM reaches terminal "unknown" within 5 s (latency recorded), execute() rejects, and the marker count is unchanged. Quote docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Lifetimes": "Detached service: independent process survives Pi client disconnect but does not guarantee service crash recovery." Quote docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Current experimental distribution": "The local detached shell tier is a separate process-lifecycle proof, not remote authentication or native crash-durability evidence."

D7. Offline falsifiers in test/workbench-detached-faults-receipt.test.ts: a journey with marker count 2 under one id -> finding "duplicate-effect"; terminal "completed" after crash -> finding "fabricated-terminal"; same-id relaunch accepted -> finding "reuse-after-loss"; sibling cancellationRequested true or terminal "cancelled" -> finding "mass-cancellation"; unresolvedEffects false for a running host -> finding "unresolved-effects-hidden"; a clean fixture -> pass true with every receipt field present; the generated provider text contains exactly one marker write before process.kill and none after. Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Each major work package must have a falsifier: a negative test that would fail if a critical guarantee was quietly weakened." Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Test classes" D: "Fault: ambiguous write timeout, process kill at every side-effect boundary, transport disconnect".

D8. Evidence-grade receipt and placement. The receipt carries contract "workbench.detached-faults/v1", utc, revision (git rev-parse HEAD or the literal "working-tree"), node, arch, platform, per-journey timestamps and latencies, markerCounts, findings, realised and pass, and contains no absolute filesystem path (basenames and invocation ids only); forge.toml gains exactly one [build.commands.local-detached-faults] block (command "node qa/workbench/local-detached-faults.mjs", timeout 240) with the [build] gate list byte-for-byte unchanged (the test asserts both); npm run build && forge run local-detached-faults is executed in the worktree and its command id, exit code and receipt are recorded in the delivered ledger line; node qa/workbench/local-detached-client.mjs still exits 0. Quote docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Every test evidence artifact includes revision, tool versions, commands, timestamp, host, native references and actual output." Quote docs/workbench/15-implementation-program.md § "Vertical cuts" VC-7: "Remote host authentication, reattachment, native immutable deployment refs, crash/uncertain-operation conformance."

D9. Gate. ./node_modules/.bin/biome check --write on the new test; npm run typecheck clean (no any, no inline imports); ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/workbench-detached-faults-receipt.test.ts test/workbench-local-detached.test.ts green; src/ unchanged (git diff --name-only shows no src/ path); never weaken or delete existing tests; do not edit docs/TRACEABILITY.md (acceptance owner reconciles).

title: W22-C: offline vendored native-SDK pin falsifier (vendor/README.md SHA-256 table == tarball bytes; package-lock file:vendor entries carry inBundle+integrity+matching version; bundledDependencies covers every file:vendor dependency; no orphan tarball)
description:
Gap: vendor/README.md publishes SHA-256 values for forge-sdk-0.1.0.tgz, furnace-sdk-0.1.0.tgz and hyperunix-sdk-0.1.0.tgz as a prose table. src/workbench/identity.ts verifies package-lock integrity against vendor bytes at invocation-identity capture time (test "pins actual package.json, package-lock.json and local vendor artifact bytes"), but nothing in the portable gate checks that (a) the README table equals the on-disk SHA-256 of each tarball, (b) every `file:vendor/*.tgz` dependency in package.json is listed in `bundledDependencies` and has a package-lock `packages["node_modules/<name>"]` entry with `resolved: "file:vendor/<file>"`, `inBundle: true`, a version matching the tarball filename and a well-formed integrity, or (c) no tarball exists without a README row and a package.json dependency (orphan). docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md § "Clean external install" records the real regression this guards: cmd_8d6d9f378d88 failed because "npm could not resolve local native SDK tarballs before extracting the parent package" until the SDKs were bundled; today that would only be caught by the network-requiring install-smoke tier.

Deliver: test/workbench-vendor-pins.test.ts (new vitest; node:crypto sha256 over vendor/*.tgz; parses the README markdown table rows `| <file> | <sha256> |`, package.json and package-lock.json; no network, no npm child process). Implement the checker as a pure function inside the test file (input: { readmeRows, tarballDigests, manifest, lock }, output: string[] of findings) so the same function runs against the real tree AND against in-memory negative fixtures: a README row with one hex digit changed -> finding naming the file and both digests; a `file:vendor/x.tgz` dependency absent from bundledDependencies -> finding; a lock entry with `inBundle: false` or a `resolved` that is not `file:vendor/<file>` -> finding; a tarball without a README row or without a package.json dependency -> orphan finding; a version in the filename that differs from the lock entry version -> finding.

Out of scope: changing vendor contents, versions, lockfile or package.json (if the real-tree run is red at rig HEAD, stop, record the mismatch in the ledger line and return blocked rather than editing pins); docs edits; src/ edits; forge.toml edits.

Files: test/workbench-vendor-pins.test.ts (new).
acceptance_criteria:
All criteria quote docs/workbench specs or vendor/README.md in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

1. docs/workbench/17-packaging-and-operations.md § "Current experimental distribution": "Native SDK artifacts are checksum-pinned and bundled so a packed parent can install them." -> for each of forge-sdk-0.1.0.tgz, furnace-sdk-0.1.0.tgz, hyperunix-sdk-0.1.0.tgz: sha256(bytes) equals the vendor/README.md table value; package.json dependencies contains `file:vendor/<file>` for the package; `bundledDependencies` includes the package; package-lock `packages["node_modules/<pkg>"]` has resolved === "file:vendor/<file>", inBundle === true, version equal to the version in the filename, and integrity matching /^sha(256|384|512)-[A-Za-z0-9+/]+={0,2}$/.
2. docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Supply chain": "Pin SDK versions, package/artifact digests and provenance." -> an in-memory fixture whose README digest differs by one hex digit yields a finding that names the file and both digests; a tarball with no README row, or no package.json dependency, yields an orphan finding; a filename/lock version disagreement yields a finding.
3. docs/workbench/14-qa-and-benchmarks.md § "Truth labels and release gates": "Pin dependencies, lockfile and package exports." and docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md § "Clean external install": "npm could not resolve local native SDK tarballs before extracting the parent package." -> a fixture with a `file:vendor/` dependency absent from bundledDependencies, or whose lock entry has inBundle false, yields a finding; the test runs inside `npm run test` (portable gate) with no network and no npm child process.
4. docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-048: "Artifact/host compatibility detects mismatched digest and rejects or explicitly migrates." -> the guard never auto-corrects: it only reports findings; nothing under vendor/ or package*.json is written (the test asserts those files' bytes are unchanged after the run).
5. vendor/README.md: "The checksums identify what this consumer installs. They do not establish that the producing checkouts were clean or that every native runtime supports every SDK method." and docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Experimental immutable receipt": "Native executable identity remains a producer-specific observation." -> assertion messages and test names say the artifact BYTES are pinned and make no claim about native executables or clean producer checkouts.

Process: red-first (negative fixtures fail before the checker exists; the real-tree assertions must be green at rig HEAD — if red, stop and report the mismatch, never edit pins); ./node_modules/.bin/biome check --write on the new test; no any; no inline imports; never weaken or delete existing tests; forge run lint / typing / test green in the worktree; do not edit docs/TRACEABILITY.md.

title: VC-6/W17-A: pure digest-pinned workflow patch proposal (bounded redacted diff, static validation of the candidate, affected pinned invocations stay unchanged, operator-only promotion receipt; never writes source or replaces a running invocation); Pi tool registration excluded
description:
Gap: src/workbench/designer.ts (hot; import-only here) ships catalogWorkflows / inspectWorkflowSource / validateWorkflowSource and the measured-cohort compareWorkflowRuns, but nothing represents designer-cycle steps C ("DESIGN a source edit and corresponding validation plan"), D ("CHECK compile/types, SDK permission bindings and expected side effects") and H ("REPORT diff ... Human/operator promotes changes explicitly") for a CANDIDATE source. docs/workbench/TRACEABILITY.md lists WB-038, WB-039 and WB-047 as "planned" with no source or test. The VC-6 journey "Pi generates a source diff improving redundant task, validates it, executes reproducible comparison and cites native results" has no artifact between "generate a diff" and "validate".

Deliver ONE new pure module and ONE new test file; register nothing; edit no existing file.

src/workbench/patch-proposal.ts (new; imports only: type WorkflowSource, type WorkflowValidation, validateWorkflowSource from ./designer.js; type DefinitionRef, type InvocationSnapshot, canonicalJson, identityDigest from ./identity.js; type CapabilityRegistry from ./capability-registry.js; redactWorkbenchText from ./redaction.js; safeWorkflowTerminalText from ../ui/workflow-card.js; createHash from node:crypto. Nothing from node:fs, node:child_process or any provider):
• PATCH_PROPOSAL_CONTRACT = "workbench.patch-proposal/v1"; class PatchProposalError extends Error { code: "SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH" | "CANDIDATE_TOO_LARGE" | "PROMOTION_PRECONDITION" | "VALIDATION" }.
• proposeWorkflowPatch(input: { base: WorkflowSource; candidateSource: string; rationale: string; hypothesis?: { metric: string; direction: "lower" | "higher"; groundedIn: readonly string[] }; pinnedInvocations?: readonly InvocationSnapshot[]; registry?: CapabilityRegistry; grants?: readonly string[]; limits?: { maxDiffLines?: number; maxPreviewBytes?: number } }): WorkflowPatchProposal.
  – First check: base.definition.artifactDigest must equal `sha256:<hex>` of base.source (same form designer.ts uses) else throw PatchProposalError("SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH") before any diff or validation work.
  – candidate.definition = { ...base.definition, artifactDigest: sha256(candidateSource) }; validation = validateWorkflowSource({ definition: candidate.definition, sourceRef: base.sourceRef, source: candidateSource }, { registry, grants }) so SOURCE_TOO_LARGE, control-character, META and possible-call/grant diagnostics are inherited unchanged and `executed` stays false.
  – diff: deterministic line diff (LCS or Myers) over base vs candidate; hunks `{ op: "context" | "add" | "remove"; baseLine?: number; candidateLine?: number; text: string }` with text = safeWorkflowTerminalText(redactWorkbenchText(line)); bounded by limits.maxDiffLines (default 400) and limits.maxPreviewBytes (default 65536) with `truncated: boolean`; `summary: { added, removed, unchanged }` counted over the FULL diff even when the preview is truncated; identical bytes -> status "no-change" with zero hunks.
  – affectedPinnedInvocations: for each pinnedInvocations entry whose scriptDigest === base.definition.artifactDigest -> { logicalInvocationId, scriptDigest, action: "unchanged", note: "remains pinned to the base digest; the candidate requires a new logical invocation" }; other snapshots are only counted in unrelatedInvocations; input snapshots are never mutated.
  – promotion: { state: "proposed"; requires: "operator"; applied: false }; experiment: { independentVariable: "source"; referenceDigest; candidateDigest; mustHold: ["inputDigest", "modelDigest", "toolsDigest", "environmentDigest", "cacheDigest"] } (the CompareRun field names, so compareWorkflowRuns can later treat source as the only intended difference); hypothesis echoed with grounding: "ungrounded" when groundedIn is empty; causalClaim: false; status: validation.status ("valid" | "invalid" | "uncertain") or "no-change"; contractVersion; proposalDigest = identityDigest("patch-proposal", <proposal without proposalDigest>).
  – Every returned object is deep-frozen plain data; JSON round-trip is lossless.
• recordPromotionDecision(proposal, decision: { decision: "promoted" | "rejected" | "deferred"; principal: { id: string; role?: string }; at: string; reason: string }): PromotionReceipt — frozen; "promoted" requires proposal.status === "valid" else throw PatchProposalError("PROMOTION_PRECONDITION"); receipt fields: contractVersion, proposalDigest, decision, principal, at, reason, appliesTo: "versioned-source", appliedByWorkbench: false, pinnedInvocationsChanged: 0. The module exports no function that accepts a filesystem path.

test/workbench-patch-proposal.test.ts (new): red-first; no TTY, provider, network or filesystem writes; uses an in-memory WorkflowSource built like test/workbench-designer.test.ts does, an InvocationSnapshot fixture from captureInvocationIdentity (identity.ts) or a literal, and a stub CapabilityRegistry for the grant case.

Out of scope: editing src/workbench/designer.ts, src/index.ts, src/workbench/redaction.ts, src/ui/workflow-card.ts or any other existing/hot file; registering a Pi tool (workflow_propose would live in hot src/index.ts); applying patches; executing candidates; comparing runs (compareWorkflowRuns exists). If the worker finds an edit to an existing file necessary to satisfy acceptance, stop and return blocked.

Files: src/workbench/patch-proposal.ts (new), test/workbench-patch-proposal.test.ts (new).
acceptance_criteria:
All criteria quote docs/workbench specs in the rig (branch workbench/implementation-program).

1. docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md § "Workflow designer cycle": "C. DESIGN a source edit and corresponding validation plan." and "D. CHECK compile/types, SDK permission bindings and expected side effects." -> proposal.validation is exactly validateWorkflowSource over the candidate bytes with the supplied registry/grants: a candidate that calls node("forge.gate.status") while grants omit the capability carries the designer's existing diagnostic in proposal.validation.diagnostics and proposal.status mirrors validation.status; validation.executed === false; a syntactically broken candidate yields status "invalid" with the designer's syntax diagnostic, never a thrown parse error.
2. docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md § "Workflow designer cycle": "No automatic rewrite of live pinned scripts." and § "Operator actions versus designer edits": "Pi can *recommend* changes without permission to apply them. Design-time edits occur against versioned source; execution against immutable digest." -> a fixture script file's bytes and mtime are unchanged after proposeWorkflowPatch and recordPromotionDecision; the module source (read by the test) contains no `node:fs` or `node:child_process` import and exports no path-taking function; promotion.applied === false and receipt.appliedByWorkbench === false on every path including "promoted".
3. docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-039: "No automatic code-edit and live replacement of already pinned running execution." and docs/workbench/08-lifecycle-and-recovery.md § "Run recovery and journal design": "Do not silently migrate a running invocation to new source/registry version." -> two pinned InvocationSnapshots on the base digest appear in affectedPinnedInvocations with action "unchanged" and are deep-equal before and after the call; a snapshot on a different digest is only counted in unrelatedInvocations; no returned field carries the candidate digest for any existing invocation.
4. docs/workbench/02-atomic-requirements.md WB-038: "Versioned plan/execute/observe comparison uses immutable source and config digest references." and docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md § "Comparative experiment protocol": "Pin workload, input revisions, workspace basis, code digest, model config, SDK versions and permissions." -> proposal.experiment.referenceDigest === base.definition.artifactDigest, candidateDigest === `sha256:` of the candidate bytes, mustHold deep-equals ["inputDigest","modelDigest","toolsDigest","environmentDigest","cacheDigest"]; a base whose artifactDigest does not match its own bytes throws PatchProposalError code SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH before any diff or validation (spy on validateWorkflowSource via a wrapper fixture, or assert via a candidate whose validation would throw).
5. docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Input and output hardening": "Validate Unicode and terminal escape sequences before display (no untrusted ANSI injection)." and docs/workbench/09-observation-and-provenance.md § "Acceptance/negative controls" item 10: "Large/secret payload does not leak into Pi tool result or screen by default." -> a candidate line containing "\x1b[31m", U+202E and "Authorization: Bearer abc123" appears in diff hunks with escape/bidi characters removed and the credential replaced by the redaction marker that redactWorkbenchText emits; a 600-changed-line candidate with maxDiffLines 400 yields truncated === true, exactly 400 hunks, and summary counts equal to the full diff; serialized hunk text never exceeds maxPreviewBytes.

description:

title: wb-g1g.1 review: evidence preview bounding cuts inside UTF-8 sequences and UTF-16 surrogate pairs (boundPreview/safeChunks), fabricating U+FFFD and lone surrogates and exceeding maxBytes by up to 2 bytes
description:
Adversarial review finding (flywheel reviewer, run g1-r3) against machine/flywheel/wb-g1g.1 @ 96b64fa (tree 9cd29f2, gate cmd_a8b4e1ffdff4). Reproduced in a detached review worktree at 96b64fa with vitest 4.1.10; probe files were deleted after the run, nothing tracked was modified.

CONFIRMED: src/workbench/evidence-loader.ts bounds preview text by raw UTF-8 bytes and by UTF-16 code units, never by code points, so the bounded preview can contain characters the evidence never contained and can exceed the per-entry byte budget.

1. boundPreview (evidence-loader.ts, `Buffer.from(part).subarray(0, remaining).toString()`): a byte cut inside a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence decodes to U+FFFD. Probe: loader preview ['漢'.repeat(1000)] with bytes 3000, store maxBytes 100 -> loaded entry whose preview content (excluding the '[truncated]' marker) is 102 bytes and whose last content line ends in U+FFFD ('漢'x33 + '�'). Measured: {"sum":113,"withoutMark":102,"maxBytes":100,"hasFFFD":true}. The bead's AC3 says "at most maxBytes per entry"; the overshoot is bounded (at most 2 bytes: a 1-byte partial replaced by a 3-byte U+FFFD) but it is a measured violation, and the U+FFFD is a glyph not present in the source.

2. safeChunks (evidence-loader.ts, `cleaned.slice(at, at + EVIDENCE_LINE_CHARS)`): slicing at 240 UTF-16 code units splits a surrogate pair when the boundary is odd relative to the pairs. Probe: preview ['a' + '😀'.repeat(130)] (261 code units) -> two chunks of lengths [240, 21]; chunk 0 ends with "\ude00\ud83d" (an unpaired high surrogate) and chunk 1 starts with "\ude00\ud83d" (an unpaired low surrogate). Measured: {"loneSurrogatePerLine":[true,true]}. Neither redactWorkbenchText, stripUnsafeText (UNSAFE_TEXT covers C0/C1 and bidi only), the loader's zero-width strip nor safeWorkflowTerminalText removes lone surrogates, so they survive into the EvidenceEntry and, in the Unicode tier, into the inspector's `add()`/`safe()` output (the ASCII tier masks them as '?'). The existing suites only exercise ASCII payloads at the byte boundary ('x'.repeat(1 MiB)) and even-length emoji-free lines, so neither case is pinned; the 107 existing cases pass.

Why it matters (quoted criteria from the bead): AC3 docs/workbench/09 "store reference/short redacted preview" -> "at most maxBytes per entry (preview bounded)"; AC4 docs/workbench/12-security.md § "Input and output hardening": "Validate Unicode and terminal escape sequences before display" and docs/workbench/10 "visible unknowns, never fabricated". A preview that shows U+FFFD or lone surrogates displays text the source never carried; the bounded view should cut on code-point boundaries and keep the byte budget exact.

Suggested fix (evidence-loader.ts only; no hot or do-not-edit file): in boundPreview, accumulate code points (for..of) while Buffer.byteLength(cp) fits `remaining`, never cut inside a sequence; in safeChunks, chunk with Array.from(cleaned) (code points) so a pair is never split; optionally strip any remaining lone surrogate in the loader's own local pass (ruling 8 already gives that pass the zero-width strip). Red-first pins in test/workbench-evidence-loader.test.ts: (a) '漢'.repeat(1000) at maxBytes 100 -> content bytes <= 100 and no U+FFFD in any line; (b) 'a'+'😀'.repeat(130) -> no lone surrogate in any chunk (regex /[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])|(?<![\uD800-\uDBFF])[\uDC00-\uDFFF]/ matches no line); plus one inspector case rendering (b) at 120x40 Unicode tier with the same assertion over every output line, visibleWidth <= width.

Relation to the open wb-g1g.1 respin (BOUNDARY 09:59:13Z ruling: unauthorized for a missing grant, branch frozen at 96b64fa until the respin lands fast-forward): this is a distinct, additive P3 defect in the same module; the owner may fold it into that respin or land it as a follow-up after wb-g1g.1 closes. Not a duplicate of wb-952 (sanitizer order / zero-width class), wb-563 (host-clock capturedAt) or the redactWorkbenchText non-idempotence P3; store-wide bead search for fffd / multibyte / subarray / byte budget returned nothing.

Positives verified by this review (not findings): existing inspector cases are byte-identical except the import line; red reproduces (2 files cannot find module without the src); mutation probe removing the scope refusal in get() fails exactly the two cross-scope tests (not vacuous); the "transport plus stale" clause of A14's title is true in behaviour (probe rendered 'unavailable: transport · stale' after disconnect) even though A14's body does not exercise it; the dialog ignores load-evidence without cancel; no hot, reserved or do-not-edit file touched; base a67bc36 descends from e797a84/ad3cf6e/2a49ef6; 0 schema-version literal hits, 0 WorkflowRunResult constructions, 0 reconcile: permissions in the diff.
